LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch, what to know and a prediction as Jacksonville heads to Baltimore to open Week 9 Imagn Images In the Week 9 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Jacksonville Jaguars . Baltimore is coming off a devastating loss to the Buffalo Bills in which Lamar Jackson returned from his ankle injury and was promptly injured on his first play of the game. The Ravens also lost backup Tyler Huntley during the contest, and they are now decimated on offense as they head into Thursday night's game. Jacksonville came off its bye last week and laid the smack down on the division rival Indianapolis Colts , winning 42-7 to improve to 5-2 on the season and further solidify their hold on the AFC South. Trevor Lawrence and the offense are rolling, and the defense has been largely excellent so far this year. Will the Jaguars take care of business on the road, or will the Ravens pull off a shocking upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Ravens vs. Jaguars live Date: Thursday, Nov. 5 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: M&T Bank Stadium (Baltimore) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Jaguars -9.5, O/U 39.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Jaguars have the ball The Jags enter this game having destroyed the Colts last week behind a monster performance from their running game. Bhayshul Tuten ran 16 times for 104 yards and a touchdown, while Chris Rodriguez carried it six times for 41 yards and another score. Rodriguez was limited in practice this week with a hand injury but will play on Thursday night. Tuten's status is up in the air after he didn't practice all week due to an ankle injury sustained against Indianapolis. He played through that injury for the rest of the game, but Jacksonville might choose to rest him here. He's a game-time decision. The Ravens are allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season, with a mere 0.8 of those yards coming before contact, according to Tru Media. Jacksonville could have some issues running the ball, especially if Tuten is out, if the Baltimore front can hold up as it has for most of the season. The Ravens did get clocked for 146 yards on the ground this past week by the Bills, but James Cook averaged south of 4.0 yards per carry. A lot of the damage was done by Ray Davis late in the game with six carries for 30 yards. Josh Allen also chipped in 30 of his own. Trevor Lawrence obviously isn't as mobile or as involved in the run game as Allen, but he can move, and if the Ravens get out of their rushing lanes, he can make things happen as a scrambler. Lawrence has played extremely well so far this season, completing 65.7% of his passes at an average of 8.5 yards per attempt, with 17 touchdowns (and a league-high 8.6% touchdown rate) against just four interceptions. Lawrence's top target is clearly Parker Washington , who splits his time fairly evenly between lining up out wide and in the slot. The Ravens are 21st in net yards per attempt allowed this season, and their cornerbacks ( Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins ) largely haven't played up to expectations. Kyle Hamilton remains excellent against both the run and pass in the slot, so one could expect Washington's route split to lean more heavily toward the outside. Jacksonville may lean toward putting him where he can line up against Humphrey, whose struggles this season have been fairly well documented. Elsewhere on the perimeter, Jakobi Meyers and, to a lesser extent, Brian Thomas Jr . and Josh Cameron are involved. Meyers and Thomas have only combined for three more targets than Washington has, though, so they are more clearly ancillary pieces in the passing game. The box-score expectations for them should be somewhat muted, but they can pop up at any time for key plays. (Thomas did score last week in his return to the full-time WR3 role, for example.) The Ravens, meanwhile, have been relatively stingy against tight ends in the passing game, allowing only 35 receptions to players at the position, so it's probably not going to be the biggest night for Brenton Strange . Tight ends do have six touchdowns against the Ravens, though, so it might be worth it to at least watch out for Strange in the red zone. When the Ravens have the ball You can throw out all of the Ravens' offensive stats. Not only is Lamar Jackson out, but so is backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. Jacoby Brissett is reportedly on the way to help, but he won't be active on Thursday night. Emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano entered the game in relief of Jackson and Huntley last Sunday and will make the start on Thursday night. Fagnano, an undrafted free agent out of UConn, went 10-of-21 for 91 yards and an interception against the Bills. He threw most of his passes to the running backs and did not connect with Zay Flowers even once. Expect the Ravens to lean heavily on Derrick Henry and the run game, but do not expect them to find much success. Henry has been struggling of late to begin with (45 carries for 156 yards and a touchdown over the last three games combined), and the Jaguars have allowed 3.4 yards per carry this season — the single-best mark in all of football. Unless Fagnano and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle pull off some kind of magic act, the Ravens are likely not going to be able to move the ball much on Thursday night. The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Now Playing Share Share Video Does Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore have any chance in 'TNF' matchup? away.headline: Jaguars-Ravens Injury Report: Why Recent History Doesn't Bode Well for Bhayshul Tuten
away.blurb: The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker. There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten. Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity. Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week. The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played. The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen. Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. But a few weeks before then, here is what Coen had to say. home.headline: Ravens injury report: Wiggins questionable for Jaguars game Thursday night
home.blurb: The Ravens’ battered offensive line should get a boost Thursday night against the Jacksonville Jaguars with starting rookie right guard Vega Ioane, who missed last week’s game against the Buffalo Bills with a knee injury, set to return. “I feel really good,” Ioane, who suffered a sprained MCL, said earlier this week. “I am confident in my ability to be able to come out.” Ravens cornerback Nate Wiggins (stinger/illness) missed Wednesday’s practice and is listed as questionable. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) was ruled out for a third straight game. For the AFC South-leading Jaguars, top running back Bhayshul Tuten could be a game-time decision, coach Liam Coen said. He didn’t practice this week because of ankle/foot injuries. Starting defensive end Travon Walker, the No.1 overall pick in 2022 who has three sacks this season, is questionable with a rib injury. Ravens’ Marlon Humphrey questions criticism, says fans ‘always freaking out’ Ravens No. 2 QB Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley out for season Ioane, the 14th overall pick this past April, did not have a designation on Wednesday’s injury report and was a full participant in both practices this week. The Ravens (4-4) will need all the help they can get up front, with undrafted rookie free agent quarterback Joe Fagnano getting his first NFL start after long-term injuries to Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley. Running back Derrick Henry has also struggled of late, averaging 3.5 yards per carry over the past two games. The Jaguars (5-2) also boast the league’s second-best scoring defense and have the top-ranked run defense. Have a news tip? home.blurb: Huntley exited the contest following the play and did not return to action, with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano finishing the game for the Ravens. Huntley was ruled out for the Ravens' Week 9 "Thursday Night Football" game against the Jacksonville Jaguars , but it now appears that his absence will extend well beyond that contest. Is Lamar Jackson out for the season? While Huntley is expected to miss the rest of the season, the Ravens have not officially ruled Jackson out the rest of the way. Jackson would not be eligible to return from IR until Week 14 at the earliest, so his ability to return may depend both on his recovery and Baltimore's ability to remain competitive in the AFC playoff race. Below is a look at the expected pecking order among the quarterbacks the Ravens will have available on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 9. The Baltimore Ravens aren't just dealing with an injury to starting quarterback Lamar Jackson . They have also lost backup quarterback Tyler Huntley long-term. Huntley suffered a turf toe injury while playing in relief of Jackson against the Buffalo Bills in Week 8. The injury occurred when Huntley was being twisted to the ground by Bills defensive tackle Ed Oliver and had his right foot plant awkwardly in the ground. Huntley's turf toe injury is expected to be season-ending, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Huntley is expected to have surgery to repair his turf toe injury, as NFL Media's Ian Rapoport reports . Rapoport also compared the injury to the one Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow dealt with in 2025, when he missed nine games because of the malady. "He faces a long road ahead," Rapoport wrote in a post to X while discussing Huntley's injury. Huntley finishes the 2026 season having posted a 1-2 record while making three starts as Jackson dealt with an ankle injury earlier in the season. The 28-year-old completed 69.1% of his passes for 727 yards, four touchdowns and one interception across five total appearances. That said, Ravens coach Jesse Minter did acknowledge Jackson's thumb injury could "potentially" be season-ending . And at the very least, the malady will land the two-time MVP on IR. "That'll be a surgery deal," Minter said when discussing Jackson's injury during a postgame news conference on Sunday, Nov. 1. "He'll go to IR. That's a tough deal." Minter was asked again for an update about Jackson's status at a Monday, Nov. 2, media availability . He told reporters the 29-year-old had not yet had surgery and that the team would have more information about his status "maybe sometime this week." home.blurb: In the same report, Dan Graziano noted the Ravens will "work to solve the problem" with Jackson out for the time being and are "open to a number of ideas" at the quarterback spot with Jacoby Brissett cited as someone they could "look into" acquiring. Bagent immediately stood out as a potential trade option for Baltimore because Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle came from the Chicago Bears where the two worked together last season. Few teams are harder to figure out right now than the Colts, even though they have acknowledged their need to sell by trading away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. Jones' availability might be even harder to figure out because head coach Shane Steichen told reporters on Monday he will remain the starting quarterback. Of the potential quarterback options mentioned by Fowler and Graziano, Brissett might be the most available. He was benched by the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday in favor of Gardner Minshew II, who led the offense to 23 points in the fourth quarter and overtime in a 33-30 victory over the Dallas Cowboys. There's no good situation for the Ravens right now because Tyler Huntley also suffered a turf toe injury that is expected to keep him out for the remainder of the season. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano is set to make his first career start on Thursday night against the Jaguars. It has not been determined if Jackson will miss the rest of the season, but an IR stint will keep him out for at least the next four weeks. The schedule does help them because they have a bye in Week 13, meaning Jackson could theoretically be back on Dec. 13 with five games remaining. Amid uncertainty about Lamar Jackson's status for the remainder of the 2026 season, the Baltimore Ravens are seeking help at quarterback prior to the trade deadline as they try to stay in the AFC playoff race. Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , some of the options the Ravens are looking at include Daniel Jones and Tyson Bagent. Jackson returned on Sunday against the Buffalo Bills after missing three games then injured his thumb on his first pass attempt. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters after the 36-10 loss to Buffalo that Jackson would undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve. The Bears may not be eager to trade Bagent since Caleb Williams has already missed time this season, though they did get one quality start from Case Keenum during Williams' absence that might make head coach Ben Johnson comfortable if he had to step in. The Colts are reportedly open to trading Jonathan Taylor, but they still played him 38 offensive snaps and risked a potential injury in Sunday's 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur announced Minshew will remain the starter going forward and rookie Carson Beck will be the No. 2, leaving Brissett as the emergency third quarterback. The Detroit Lions defeated the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings , the Denver Broncos used a goal-line stand to hand Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs their second consecutive loss, and the Chicago Bears upset the Seahawks in Seattle with some help from trade-deadline addition Jeffery Simmons . This weekend in the NFL , the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons will battle in Madrid, Jordan Love takes the Green Bay Packers to Foxborough to play the New England Patriots and Baker Mayfield gets a shot at Caleb Williams and the red-hot Bears. Which teams should you pick in Week 9, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 4 from DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research for its hard work. Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens (TNF) Dajani ( Jaguars -10): It's tough to pick this game since we are unaware of the Baltimore Ravens ' quarterback situation. Will they be starting rookie third-stringer Joe Fagnano , or someone else? I believe the Jaguars will win, but any team can cover a double-digit spread at home. Jacksonville is a remarkable 14-3 over its last 17 games and is the only NFL team leading its division by three or more games. Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in passer rating (112.6), while the Jags lead the league in points per game differential (+12.1). Sure, you can say the Ravens will just ride Derrick Henry , but the Jaguars have what is statistically the No. 1 run defense in the NFL, and have gone 24 straight games without allowing a 75-yard rusher. … Prediction: Jaguars 28, Ravens 13 Dubin (Jaguars -10): The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. … Prediction: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) vs. Atlanta Falcons (Madrid) Dajani (Falcons +3): I may take the upset here. I'm aware the Falcons just registered one of the most embarrassing losses of the season in Tampa, but I'm willing to overlook that given how bad the weather was. I have some questions about the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner has a heel injury, and Cashius Howell just broke his wrist. Then, this Cincy defense allowed the lowly Tennessee Titans to put up 440 yards of total offense last week and allowed the first Titans' 300-yard passing game since the 2023 season. Tony Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns, so what is Bijan Robinson going to do? Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best wide receiving duo in the league, but the Bengals may be due for their first loss in over a month. Remember, this Falcons team beat the San Francisco 49ers the last time they played a game indoors. Give me the points. … Prediction: Falcons 27, Bengals 23 Dubin (Bengals -3): The Cincinnati offense is rolling, with Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dunking on opposing defenses. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been struggling to run the ball as of late despite the presence of Bijan Robinson (48 carries for 200 scoreless yards in the last three weeks). The Bengals do provide an opportunity for the run game to get back on track (4.8 yards per carry allowed), but Dexter Lawrence has shut down other rushing attacks before. If the Bengals can keep Robinson in check, I'm not sure Atlanta can count on Michael Penix Jr . to go shot for shot with Burrow. … Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 20 Los Angeles Rams (-5.5) at Washington Commanders Dajani ( Rams -5.5): I think the Washington Commanders are a feisty team that could cover this number, but don't forget that this is somewhat of a revenge game for Sean McVay. He spent seven seasons in Washington before the Rams made the smart decision to hire this 30-year-old kid to run their franchise. In his first season as a head coach, McVay lost to his former team. Since then, he's 2-0 vs. Washington, winning each game by at least eight points. The Rams are coming off back-to-back wins by 14+ points. They also could get Myles Garrett back on Sunday. LA is 11-2 SU and 10-3 ATS in its last 13 games vs. teams entering below .500. … Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 17 Dubin (Rams -5.5): The Rams have finally climbed back to .500 with back-to-back wins over the Raiders and Chargers , and I think they can keep things rolling here by doing what they did against those two teams: running the ball. Washington has actually been pretty good against the ground game this year, but it just lost Daron Payne to a significant injury. On the other side of the ball, I don't think we can count on the Commanders' offense to produce enough points to keep up with LA's offense. … Prediction: Rams 24, Commanders 16 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Dajani (Broncos -2.5): I told you the Broncos would beat the Chiefs last week. The conversation around Bo Nix is so bizarre to me. He's not Josh Allen , obviously, but he's not worth benching either. He's not the most prolific passer in NFL history, but he's Superman when it comes to leading his team to wins in crunch time. Denver does have a great defense, which pulled off that goal-line stand vs. Kansas City, but Nix leads the NFL since 2000 with 9.1 yards per attempt when down by one score in the fourth quarter. He has 15 game-winning drives to his name, which is one shy of the most in a three-season span in NFL history. Nix hasn't even played three full seasons. It hasn't always been pretty, but Nix is pretty good in those fourth quarters. This week, Denver travels to take on the Carolina Panthers . Bryce Young 's offensive line has some serious issues, and those were evident last week against the Packers. Through Week 8, Carolina has allowed 23 sacks, which is tied for second-most in the NFL, with 11 of those sacks coming in the past two games. Plus, the Panthers' defense has allowed an incredible 42.7 points per contest in their first three home games, which eventually led to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero last week. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Panthers 20 Dubin (Broncos -2.5): I'm not buying into Nix as much as Dajani is, but I am buying into Denver's defense being able to get after Bryce Young behind what is an increasingly leaky offensive line and preventing the Panthers from denting the scoreboard. If they can keep this a low-scoring game, I like them to pull out a win on the road. … Prediction: Broncos 23, Panthers 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (-3) Dajani (Packers +3): The Packers got some extra rest following their Thursday win over Carolina, while the New England Patriots couldn't run away from the Miami Dolphins . This Packers offense has been fun to watch — not counting the ground game, which has registered the fewest rushing yards (485) by a team above .500 through eight games in NFL history. However, Jordan Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards, while Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first duo to have 600 yards receiving each through eight games since Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill in 2022! Drake Maye has been great, having scored at least three touchdowns over five straight games, but this Packers defense will provide quite the test. Green Bay has allowed just 14.6 points per game over its last five. … Prediction: Packers 27, Patriots 24 Dubin (Packers +3): I also think Green Bay's extra rest will matter here, even if only because it will give Christian Watson some extra time to heal up from the ribs injury he suffered last Thursday night. The Packers are going to need him against New England, even if he ends up drawing shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez , as that will just open things up for Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft . Meanwhile, Green Bay's defense has been excellent for several weeks now, and with the Patriots down multiple weapons in the passing game, I think the Packers can try to make New England one-dimensional here, limiting their chances to move the ball downfield. … Prediction: Packers 26, Patriots 20 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears (-6) (SNF) Dajani (Bears -6): I correctly chose Chicago to cover in Seattle last week, and I became even more confident in that pick when the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons. The Seahawks' addition of Quenton Nelson is a great one, but I think the addition of Simmons is even better. He's the best defensive tackle in the NFL and makes life incredibly difficult for quarterbacks. In his first game for his new team, he recorded six tackles, one sack and two tackles for loss. Chicago's defense allowed just 3.0 yards per play with him

Then it went rotten — at least with my against-the-spread NFL picks , I went into the late games with a 6-3 ATS record. I ended up 7-7 for the week. That takes my season record to a horrible 50-68-3. As for my straight-up picks, I went 10-4. That brings my season record to 72-48-1. That I will take. Now it's time to get going on the ATS record. I went with some strange dogs this week in hopes of getting back on track. Let's hope they bark. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Jaguars get a break on a short week, not having to face Lamar Jackson at quarterback. The Ravens are a different team without him and now must play rookie Joe Fagnano . Trevor Lawrence is playing at a high level and the run game is going well. Look for the Jaguars to win a road game on a short week. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 16 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Madrid on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals have been flying high on offense with Joe Burrow throwing it around. The Falcons have struggled on offense in recent weeks, which is never a good thing when trying to keep up with Burrow. Look for a lot more big plays from the Bengals as they win this one in Spain. Pick: Bengals 33, Falcons 21 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix . This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line. Pick: Broncos 26, Panthers 20 Dallas Cowboys (-6) at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys are coming off a horrible loss to the Cardinals at home, but they get a big break playing the Colts , who are struggling. Indianapolis has major problems and there is talk of trading more players. The Cowboys will get the offense cranked up again in this one as they get back on track behind their passing game. Pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 17 New York Jets (+9.5) at Kansas City Chiefs The Chiefs are back home after losing two straight on the road. The Jets blew a late lead to the Raiders last week. Kansas City has not run it the past two weeks, but look for Kenneth Walker to get back on track. The Chiefs win it to break the losing streak, but the Jets and their offense hang around. Pick: Chiefs 24, Jets 17 Detroit Lions (-7) at Miami Dolphins This is a tough trip for the Lions coming off two home division victories, and it's against a young team playing much better. But this is a big challenge for the Miami defense. The Lions can score in bunches and I think they will in this one. Look for a big day from Jared Goff . Pick: Lions 30, Dolphins 13 Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints (-1.5) The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. Pick: Saints 17, Browns 14 New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles (+3.5) The Giants are coming off a bye in first place in the division, while the Eagles are coming off a road loss Sunday night to the Commanders . They are struggling in many areas. But this is a big rivalry, and pride will help keep the Eagles in it, as their defense has a solid day against J.J. McCarthy . But the Giants win it late. Pick: Giants 22, Eagles 20 Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders (+5.5) This is a long trip for the Rams , but they seemed to have righted things the past few weeks. The Commanders rallied to beat the Eagles Sunday night. The Washington defense played well in that game, but this could be a game where Matt Stafford gets it cranked up. Jayden Daniels will play well to keep it close, but the Rams will win it. Pick: Rams 28, Commanders 24 Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Texans are coming off a bye, while the Chargers are coming off a loss to the Rams. Neither team has come close to expectations before the season, with the Chargers winless. The Texans' defense and the Chargers' offense have both struggled. But I think the Chargers will hang around in this one behind their defense. Pick: Texans 19, Chargers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, while the 49ers are coming off a bye. Big edge for the 49ers. Plus, they are the better team. The Raiders' defense is struggling, so look for Brock Purdy to have a big day throwing the football. 49ers big. Pick: 49ers 31, Raiders 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (+3.5) This has the feel of a low-scoring game with two good defenses — even though both teams have good quarterbacks. The Packers have added rest from playing last Thursday, which will help. The Patriots had to rally and beat the Dolphins last week. The defenses play well, but It's Jordan Love who makes the plays late to win it. Pick: Packers 19, Patriots 16 Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks (-12.5) The Seahawks are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the Bears , while the Cardinals won at Dallas last week. They are making a quarterback change to Gardner Minshew , who played well last week. Good luck against this Seattle defense, which will be hunting after the Bears beat them. The Cardinals will get the brunt of their anger. Pick: Seahawks 30, Cardinals 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are coming off that impressive victory over Seattle Monday night on the road. That was domination. But there might be a little letdown here. The Bucs have played impressive defense this season and have cranked up their running game. They will run it well here, but in the end, Caleb Williams will make late plays to win it. Pick: Bears 24, Bucs 21 Buffalo Bills (-3.5) at Minnesota Vikings Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the game of the week, featuring two of the better teams in the league. I can't wait to see the Vikings ' defense against Josh Allen . But I think the Bills will run the ball at the Minnesota defense, much like the Lions did last week. The Bills defense has been better as of late, and that will show up against a limited Minnesota offense. The Cincinnati Bengals need extra luggage to carry all their momentum to Madrid, aiming to extend their winning ways versus the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday morning. Cincinnati is laying just over a field goal inside Santiago Bernabéu Stadium, riding a three-game streak into Week 9 but building that run against some softer opposition. My Bengals vs. Falcons predictions size up the edges for this international encounter, giving my best NFL picks to wake up to on Nov. 8, starring Tee Higgins. Bengals vs Falcons prediction: Falcons +3.5 The Cincinnati Bengals are rolling right now, but those victories have come against some weaker opponents. They took down bottom-feeders like Miami and Tennessee (barely), while needing a second-half rally to overcome Baltimore and a backup QB. There was also a bye in Week 6 giving Cincy a breather. I believe the Bengals should be the favorites in Spain, but not by this many points. The Atlanta Falcons are coming off a strange Week 8 loss in which weather played a huge role in the result. That included four interceptions from QB Michael Penix Jr. , who had only one INT in the previous five starts. I'm not discounting Atlanta too much for that rain-soaked squash at Tampa Bay. Rather, I see the Falcons facing one of the easier defenses on their recent schedule, with the Bengals stop unit slipping the past three games. The most notable dip has come defending the run. The Bengals are allowing 5.1 yards per carry in their last three outings (second most in the NFL). Not what you want to see when staring down Bijan Robinson . Bengals vs Falcons combo The Bengals should be favorites, but their current three-game win streak is very puffed up, and Atlanta poses a stiffer test on a neutral field. I'll take Atlanta on the other side of a field goal. Chase Brown hasn't found paydirt since Week 1. The Falcons have given up 11 total touchdowns to running backs and Brown is a dual-threat option, either running it past the goal line or catching a TD strike. Tee Higgins could be the best WR2 in the league. He's the top-rated WR versus man coverage and faces plenty of one-on-one coverage from Atlanta. Projections call for another big day, with most models north of 80 yards receiving from Higgins. Chase Brown touchdown Tee Higgins 75+ receiving yards TOP PICK Bengals vs Falcons player prop: Tee Higgins 75+ receiving yards Bengals receiver Tee Higgins is coming off a monster day versus Tennessee, drawing 11 targets for 10 catches and 155 yards. Higgins could be the best WR2 in the league, with Ja'Marr Chase drawing the ire of the secondary and leaving the 6-foot-4 Higgins with softer matchups. He gets a perfect pairing against Atlanta in Madrid. The Falcons rank 24th in DVOA defending WR2s , allowing an average of 54.6 yards per game to the position. This secondary is also running a high rate of man coverage (10th most), and Higgins currently rates as the No. 1 WR versus man at PFF. Projections for Higgins range from 74 to 88 yards on Sunday morning, with most models north of 80 yards. My number comes out to 81.5 receiving yards in Madrid. Want more NFL player props? They are both in extremely tight division races where just one win could propel them into first place. However, the difference between the AFC North and the NFC South is absolutely massive. Still, the Falcons have looked impressive at times throughout the season. Meanwhile, the Bengals have been fairly consistent now that their defense is finally looking solid. Joe Burrow has a repeat of his Week 8 offensive explosion against the Falcons Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports The Bengals looked like a vintage version of the team in Week 8 against the Dolphins. Yes, Cincinnati did get the win. But it was shocking how much they needed to lean on Burrow to get the job done. Fortunately, Burrow is one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL and passed that tough test with flying colors. Burrow finished 38-of-48 for 462 passing yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions. He also had one rushing touchdown. The veteran quarterback simply put the team on his back and willed them to victory. Now Burrow and friends must face an average Falcons defense that's allowed 223.4 passing yards per game this season. Keep in mind that the best opponent Atlanta has faced this season is Chicago. In that game, Caleb Williams shredded their secondary for 305 passing yards. Beyond that game, the Falcons have not been tested very much through the air this season. So just how much damage could Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins do against the Falcons? Burrow will have a repeat performance from last week, going over 400 passing yards and throwing at least three touchdown passes. Cincinnati has to throw the ball to win right now, so they'll be comfortable going guns blazing. To make this even bolder, both Higgins and Chase will each go over 100 receiving yards and score a touchdown. Bijan Robinson will have twice as many rushing yards as the Bengals The disparity between Atlanta and Cincinnati's running game is absolutely massive. Cincinnati has one of the worst rushing attacks in the entire league. In fact, they only average 80.3 rushing yards per game so far this season. That average is quite concerning since they've already played in seven games, so a few bad performances aren't dragging it down. Chase Brown and company just aren't getting the job done. Atlanta is the exact opposite, with their Bijan Robinson-led rushing attack as one of the best in the NFL. They've averaged 134.8 rushing yards per game this year. Only the Buccaneers, Bears, and Bills have a better average. Robinson is the main reason why the Falcons have such a huge advantage on the ground. Just how good will he do in comparison to the Bengals in Madrid? Bijan is averaging 100.6 rushing yards per game in 2026. He is single-handedly outperforming the Bengals on the ground despite failing to break 100 rushing yards in four consecutive games. Mayfield guided the Bucs to their second win of the season against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7, and oddsmakers are buying the Buccaneers at home in Week 8 against the Atlanta Falcons. The Buccaneers are favored to win their matchup with the Falcons, sitting as 2.5-point favorites in the odds at DraftKings Sportsbook . After a 1-5 start to the season, Tampa Bay's win over Carolina thrust it back into the mix to win the division this season. Another win over an NFC South opponent would go a long way for Tampa Bay getting into the playoffs, and the running game has really stepped forward in recent weeks with both Mayfield and Jalon Daniels under center. Mayfield wasn't asked to do much against Carolina, completing just seven of his 11 passes for 76 yards and a score. He's completed 63.6 percent of his passes for 679 yards, three scores and two picks in four games. Daniels led Tampa Bay to one win while Mayfield was sidelined, but it's pretty clear that oddsmakers view the former No. 1 overall pick as a major upgrade under center. Mayfield and the Bucs take on Altanta and Chicago over the next two weeks before their bye. Atlanta is currently one game ahead of Tampa Bay in the NFC South, but a win on Sunday would vault the Bucs into second in the divison, just a half-game back of the Panthers (3-4). You probably don't need me to tell you how that turned out. In similar fashion, I got crushed on my three bold takes for last week's game . I vow to bounce back this week, just like the Cowboys will hopefully do. The Cowboys are on the road for this week's game against the Indianapolis Colts, and are 5.5-point favorites, according to our friends at FanDuel. The over/under is 51.5 points. The Cowboys being favored is more an indictment of the Colts than anything else. On to the bold predictions for the Cowboys versus Colts. Colts QBs run for 75+ yards The headline says Colts QBs for two reasons. One is Daniel Jones, and his backup Anthony Richardson, have wheels, and it feels likely the Colts may try to pull a "Cardinals switcheroo" on the Cowboys if Jones gets off to a rough start. So both Jones and Richardson could get reps in the game. Secondly, the Cowboys defense is never able to contain mobile quarterbacks. It's just not in their DNA. So Jones alone, or maybe in combination with Richardson, will go for over 75 yards on the ground. George Pickens gets a 40+ yards TD There is no real scheme-related thing for this bold prediction. Just a feeling. Cowboys fandom is frustrated with how Brian Schottenheiemer is using Pickens. The receiver himself is likely getting frustrated at the lack of action. Trade rumors have been attached to his name. That's a lot of noise. To quiet it all down, the Cowboys will feature Pickens more, and one of those targets will pay off big with a 40+ yard touchdown. away.blurb: Sunday’s matchup at Lucas Oil Stadium brings together two teams badly in need of a reset, as the Dallas Cowboys (3-5) visit the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. home.headline: Latest Dallas Cowboys injury report brings worrying news for a banged-up defense ahead of Week 9 matchup with Colts
home.blurb: The Dallas Cowboys are running out of healthy bodies in the secondary with the Indianapolis Colts coming to town. And a key defender popped up on the injury report out of nowhere. When Porter Jr. was a participant on Wednesday, those concerns eased a bit. On Thursday, however, the Cowboys listed him as a limited participant again. Speaking of the secondary, safeties Caleb Downs and PJ Locke remain in the concussion protocol. Each was upgraded from a non-participant on Wednesday to a limited participant on Thursday. NFL players who enter the protocol often miss at least one week, but there's no set minimum number of days a player has to sit. In 2023, CBS Sports insider Jonathan Jones reported that the median return from a concussion is nine days. At least Downs and Locke took a significant step forward by getting back to on-field activity as limited participants. Sticking with the defense, linebacker DeMarvion Overshown is a new addition to the report. He wasn't listed on Wednesday, but he was limited on Thursday with a hamstring/back injury. Overshown didn't play from Week 1 against the New York Giants until he returned against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7. Seeing him back on the injury report isn't encouraging. It doesn't necessarily mean he'll be out on Sunday. As for the rest of the linebacker group, Dee Winters continues to trend in the right direction. He was upgraded to a full participant on Thursday’s practice and is in line to return to the active roster. Wide receiver George Pickens remains on the report after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday. He's now listed with only a hamstring injury, not a shoulder injury. At tight end, Luke Schoonmaker was limited again on Thursday. He missed the last game against the Cardinals with a groin injury, and his status for Week 9 might matter more than expected. Jake Ferguson missed his second straight practice of the week after getting hurt early against Arizona. Elsewhere, edge rusher Malachi Lawrence and returner KaVontae Turpin were non-participants. Offensive tackle Tyler Smith was limited on both Wednesday and Thursday with an ankle injury, but the Cowboys didn't appear concerned about his availability for Week 9. home.headline: Cowboys HC shares 'hopeful' George Pickens injury update for Week 9 vs. Colts
home.blurb: "Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer with some injury updates on @1053thefan: CB Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) and WR George Pickens (hamstring) will be a little bit limited, but 'hopeful' they're able to play Sunday vs. Indianapolis," Yarrish shared. This isn't a very confident update, as Schottenheimer didn't come out and say both players will play in Week 9. But the fact that he's "hopeful" to have both is a good sign that Pickens and Porter can suit up this week. Both remain questionable, and there's a good chance it will stay that way as the Cowboys reveal their final injury report for this Colts matchup. This is a good update on Pickens, as he's not been ruled out. But the uncertainty, even as the Cowboys have hope he'll play, is something worth monitoring during the team's final practice Friday and leading up to their Week 9 matchup against the Colts. Cowboys HC shares 'hopeful' George Pickens injury update for Week 9 vs. Colts - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Matt Sullivan · The Sporting News Fri, November 6, 2026 at 3:06 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Dallas Cowboys , following an embarrassing overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals , are in desperate need of a win in Week 9 over the Indianapolis Colts . If they somehow lost, it would be a devastating setback. Even though the Cowboys are 3-5, the 4-2-1 New York Giants are within striking distance in the NFC East. They need a win this week. A key to winning this Week 9 game against the Colts will be the Cowboys' health, which has become a bit of a problem. However, fortunately for Dallas, Cowboys beat writer Tommy Yarrish shared a "hopeful" update on George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr. amid their injury issues, according to head coach Brian Schottenheimer. Cowboys 'hopeful' to have Pickens, Porter in Week 9 In normal circumstances, it might make sense for the Cowboys to believe they can beat the hapless Colts without both players. But after losing to the Cardinals in Week 8, they cannot take anything lightly. MORE : Jerry Jones defends Brian Schottenheimer after Cowboys collapse vs. Cardinals Pickens and Porter are linked, not just due to their roots with the Pittsburgh Steelers , but also because they are both set to hit free agency this offseason, presenting a bit of a problem for the Cowboys. There have been some trade rumors surrounding Pickens this season, and a loss to the Colts might be what pushes Jerry Jones to actually trade Pickens this season. But before such a decision could come to fruition, the Cowboys need to see if Pickens is good to go, which is something they're currently "hopeful" about. After a 5-0 start to the season, the Chiefs have lost in Seattle and in Denver in the last two weeks. They’re 3-0 at home, though, and host the lowly Jets this week. New York has wins against the Titans and Browns so far this season. The Jets have lost three straight since that victory over Cleveland. Using the latest odds and analysis, here’s where I’m leaning for this Week 9 matchup with a final score prediction. Jets vs. Chiefs Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Jets +10 (-112) Chiefs -10 (-108) 47.5 (Over -108/Under -112) Line Movement: The spread hasn’t moved since the odds opened for this game, but the total has gone up a few points from 43.5 to 47.5. Jets vs. Chiefs Final Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan broke down this game in his Road to 272 Bets column, in which he picks each game every week: I think the Jets are a better team than you think they are at first glance. Their offense ranks 13th in weighted EPA per play and 10th in offensive success rate. Their defense has struggled, ranking 21st in opponent weighted EPA per play, but they've done a solid job of stopping the run this season, allowing just 4.0 yards per carry. If they can slow down the Chiefs' run game, they're going to be in a great spot to keep this game within range. I haven't seen enough from Kansas City to bet them to win by double digits against an underrated Jets team. Pick: Jets +10 (-114) via BetRivers There are only a few situations in which I’d lay double-digit points with the Chiefs, and this isn’t one of them. Kansas City has struggled in recent weeks, and while New York has lost three straight, they were all one-score games. In fact, the Jets only have one loss by more than 10 points this season, falling 23-12 in Chicago on Oct. 4. Delane is said to be dealing with a shoulder injury, Woods has what is being described as a "neck stinger," and Norman-Lott is working his way back from a stint on injured reserve caused by his knee. While Delane and Norman-Lott were able to practice in a limited capacity over the past three days, Woods was the only Chiefs player who was held out of all of Kansas City's workouts in Week 9. Clearly, Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo will have to get creative in adjusting his game plan in the absence of Delane, Woods, and Norman-Lott as Kansas City prepares to face New York with a chance to earn its sixth win of the 2026 NFL regular season. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty Nick Roesch · HEAVY Fri, November 6, 2026 at 10:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs have wrapped their final practice of the week ahead of their showdown against the New York Jets on Sunday. Both teams are looking to snap losing streaks with a win. The Jets have already ruled out star wide receiver Garrett Wilson, and now the Chiefs have ruled out a pair of rookie starters. Kansas City Chiefs CB Mansoor Delane Out vs. Jets in Week 9 While addressing the media on Friday afternoon, coach Andy Reid stated that cornerback Mansoor Delane will not play against New York. This will be the second consecutive game Delane has missed, as he sat out during last week's loss to the Denver Broncos . Delane aggravated a shoulder injury last week that has plagued him since back in OTAs. He missed nearly all of Week 1 and the entirety of Week 2 with the issue. On a positive note, Delane did do some work in practice this week. A few days ago, Reid said it's a matter of keeping the shoulder strong enough to absorb impact. Starting in Delane's place will be veteran Kristian Fulton, who has played well when called upon this season. DT Peter Woods Also Ruled Out vs. Jets Reid also revealed that defensive tackle Peter Woods will miss Week 9's matchup against the Jets. Woods injured his neck early in the game against Denver last week. Reid described it as a "stinger," and it is not expected to be a long-term problem. Woods did not participate in any practice this week. Like Delane, the Chiefs selected Woods in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Woods hasn't made as much of an impact as Delane, but that was to be expected. With Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga ahead of him, Woods has been in a limited rotational role so far this season. Woods has a half sack, still searching for his first full career sack. Kansas City's defense as a whole is struggling to bring down opposing quarterbacks. It has just eight sacks on the season, tied for the least in the NFL. Only defensive end George Karlaftis has more than one sack. Jones has recorded just a half sack, and Tonga has zero. Defensive ends Felix Anudike-Uzomah and Ashton Gillote have posted one a piece. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images MacGregor Wells · SB Nation Mon, November 2, 2026 at 4:57 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Jets lost their third straight game and sixth of their last seven on Sunday. Last week the Jets lost at home against the previously winless Miami Dolphins. This week the Las Vegas Raiders broke their own four game losing streak by out-scoring the Jets in a wild 38 – 33 shootout in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Jets took a nine point lead into the locker room at halftime, only to unravel in the second half. The Jets defense was helpless to stop the Raiders attack in the second half as the Jets were out-scored 24 – 10 to close the game. It was a humiliating performance by a putrid Jets defense. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-6 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Any hopes of a playoff run are all but gone. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. Now the Jets go on the road to face the 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs in Kansas City next Sunday. The Chiefs have lost two straight games to tough opponents on the road. This week the Denver Broncos barely survived as the Chiefs were stopped on the one yard line as they were trying for a game winning score as time ran out. The Chiefs opened the 2026 season with a dominant 31 – 10 victory over the Denver Broncos. They followed that impressive win with four straight victories over some of the worst teams in the NFL – the Indianapolis Colts, Miami Dolphins, Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Chargers. The 5-0 start to the season was great, but with four of the wins coming against bad teams, it is tough to say just how good the Chiefs are. Now they have lost two straight to tough opponents. Are the Chiefs a top team? Maybe. It's not entirely clear. What is crystal clear is the Chiefs are a far, far better team than the Jets. Teams like the Dolphins and the Raiders have snapped their losing streaks against the Jets in East Rutherford. It seems all but inevitable Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs will do the same at home. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Unsurprisingly the oddsmakers think the Chiefs will easily handle the Jets. The current line has the Jets road underdogs by 9.5 points. The game has an over/under of 46.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +400 while the Chiefs are -520. Any given Sunday and all that jazz, but an upset here seems like a bridge too far for the Jets. Perhaps they can at least pull off one of those infamous moral victories and keep the game competitive against a Chiefs team that may understandably have trouble getting up for a game against the hapless Jets. picks.blurb: Latest Teams On Air Listen + Watch Contests Events More LISTEN LIVE Home Gang Green will visit Arrowhead Stadium in Missouri for only the second time since 2016 the Kansas City Chiefs welcome the New York Jets this Sunday afternoon at 1 p.m…. Kurt Boyer Updated Nov 6, 2026 12:24 PM EST Al Bello/Getty Images Share this story Gang Green will visit Arrowhead Stadium in Missouri for only the second time since 2016 the Kansas City Chiefs welcome the New York Jets this Sunday afternoon at 1 p.m. ET. The Jets were one good fourth quarter away from improving to .500, and now they're mired at 2-6. New York trailed just 17-13 going into the fourth quarter in New England on Oct. 18, but wound up losing to the Patriots 26-19 in an outcome that began the Jets' active three-game losing skid. The Jets are producing only 320 yards per game on average, ranking 25th in the NFL in both point-scoring and rush defense. The Kansas City Chiefs are 5-2 and favored to win at home on Sunday. But that doesn't mean that KC has any more momentum than the ailing Jets. QB Pat Mahomes' team is on a two-game losing skid, having blown a fourth-quarter lead to fall to rival Denver 28-24 last weekend. Mahomes struggled throughout KC's previous loss to Seattle, helping to finally lower O/U totals on Chiefs games. New York Jets +9.5 (49%) Kansas City Chiefs -9.5 (52%) New York Jets +350 Kansas City Chiefs -461 Over 47.5 (51%) Under 47.5 (50%) Note: The above data was compiled from prediction market platforms on Nov 6, 2026, and may have changed since writing. New York Jets at Kansas City Chiefs Betting Trends The Kansas City Chiefs have won four of the last five meetings. The Jets are 1-8 in the last nine regular-season road games. Kansas City has won three consecutive home games. New York Jets at Kansas City Chiefs Injury Reports New York Jets Running back Breece Hall is questionable with a quadriceps injury. Defensive tackle Harrison Phillips is questionable with an ankle injury. Linebacker Marcelino McCrary-Ball is out with an ankle injury. Defensive tackle David Onyemata is out with a groin injury. Defensive end Tyler Baron is out with a knee injury. Guard Anez Cooper is out with a shoulder injury. Kansas City Chiefs Tight end Travis Kelce is probable with an ankle injury. Wide receiver Nikko Remigio is questionable with a hip injury. Running back Mansoor Delane is questionable with a shoulder injury. Defensive tackle Peter Woods is questionable with a neck injury. Cornerback L'Jarius Sneed is out with a knee injury. Running back Brashard Smith is out with a hamstring injury. Offensive tackle Josh Simmons is out with a back injury. New York Jets at Kansas City Chiefs Predictions and Picks What's got the Kansas City Chiefs cooling down with the Missouri weather? The KC media believes that the Chiefs should be 6-1, and that the question of a potential slump ought to be a moot point. Mahomes thought he had thrown the winning TD pass to WR Rashee Rice with time running out in Denver, but offensive tackle Jaylon Moore was flagged for a false-start penalty on a head-turn which was not “significant enough” to warrant a penalty, as summarized by Nick Roesch's report in Heavy . Rice's bizarre bankruptcy filing was a distraction this week. The defense of a team that's distracted by controversy should be able to outplay a snakebitten offense, at least most of the time. Yet, it was arguably the Chiefs defense that let Kansas City down the worst in Colorado. They allowed the Broncos to go 2-of-2 on fourth-down conversions and 3-of-3 in the red zone. Quarterback Geno Smith of the Jets could attack a defense that's allowing 222.9 passing YPG. The key to the Jets-Chiefs betting outcome is the ground game of New York's tailback Braelon Allen, who is averaging a superb 5.0 YPC. He'll go up against a Kansas City rush defense that's surrendered only 674 yards thus far. If the Jets have a hard time running the ball, the Chiefs are likely to cover. away.headline: Jets announce concerning injury update on WR Garrett Wilson
away.blurb: The New York Jets could be without their No. 1 wide receiver weapon in Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. When speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn announced that Garrett Wilson is in the NFL ‘s concussion protocol and considered “day-to-day” moving forward. “Garrett, he’s in the concussion protocol. He’ll be day-to-day,” Glenn said. Wilson, who’s been openly frustrated about his role in the Jets’ offense so far this season, had six catches for 83 yards in this past Sunday’s 38-33 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. Wilson’s practice status later this week will be a good indication of his potential availability for Sunday’s road matchup against the Chiefs. Fortunately for the Jets, wide receiver Adonai Mitchell is back from injury and performing at a high level. In Sunday’s loss to the Raiders, he paced New York with seven catches for 142 yards and a touchdown. Rookie pass catcher Omar Cooper Jr. has also flashed brilliance on a few occasions in his debut campaign. Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the Chiefs will kick off at 1 p.m. ET from Arrowhead Stadium. picks.headline: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Miami Dolphins in Week 9
picks.blurb: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Miami Dolphins in Week 9 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Detroit Lions will head down South to take on the 1-6 Miami Dolphins this Sunday. Led by first-year head coach Jeff Hafley, the Dolphins have struggled to do much right in 2026. Through seven games, they've scored the second-fewest points (16.7/contest), plus they've allowed the ninth-most points (25.9/game). Additionally, Miami did not notch its first win of the season until Week 7, defeating Aaron Glenn and the N.Y. Jets, 28-25. Undeniably, it's been a rough season for Hafley & Co., which find themselves in possession of the third-worst record in the NFL. The only teams which have been worse are the Tennessee Titans (1-7) and the L.A. Chargers (0-7). The Lions, under Dan Campbell, were once in the same unenviable shoes as the Dolphins. When Campbell first took over in the Motor City in 2021, Detroit was far from one of the most formidable teams in the NFL. Instead, just like the Dolphins currently, Campbell & Co. experienced their fair share of struggles and lost plenty of games on their way to establishing their tough, gritty identity. In fact, Detroit started the aforementioned campaign 0-10-1 before winning its first game in Week 13 against the Minnesota Vikings. In that sense, Campbell sees plenty of parallels between those Lions and this current iteration of Miami. “Coach Hafley’s done a good job in his first year,” the sixth-year Lions head man expressed to reporters this week. “A lot of similarities — it reminds me of what we were when we came in. They’re young, they’re hungry, they’re active, they run, they hit, they hustle, they finish, try to play disciplined ball. And they’re playing that way.” As much as Campbell's squad is undoubtedly the better team, you can't take anyone lightly in the NFL. And for as bad as the Dolphins have been, it's important to note they have not lost a game by more than seven points since Week 4. Their last double-digit loss came in Week 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs (24-10). And on top of all that, the Lions are severely banged up entering this Week 9 matchup , after suffering a plethora of injuries a week ago against Minnesota. They lost five total defensive players in the divisional tilt, including defensive captain Jack Campbell, the two best members of their secondary (Brian Branch and D.J. Reed) and EDGE DJ Wonnum. The folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -7 points . The Dolphins made a general manager and head coaching change this offseason, firing GM Chris Grier and coach Mike McDaniel after four unsuccessful seasons and hiring Jon-Eric Sullivan as their new GM and former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley as their new coach. Like most new regimes, the new staff got to work early, cutting veteran contracts, including quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and edge rusher Bradley Chubb. They also traded away former first-round pick Jaylen Waddle for a trio of picks to use in the 2026 NFL Draft to help them with the rebuild. Step one in establishing a new foundation was signing Malik Willis as their new signal caller—who most recently played in Green Bay with Hafley—and drafting six (!) rookie starters, including first-round picks guard Kadyn Proctor and corner Chris Johnson, as well as second-round pick linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, third-round receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, and fifth-round safety Michael Taaffe. They also have another eight rookies on their 53-man roster, meaning over 25% of the Dolphins roster (14 players) is made up of first-year players. As you would expect with a young roster at the beginning of a rebuild, the Dolphins have struggled out of the gate. In Week 1, the Raiders beat them by two touchdowns; the 49ers won by three touchdowns the week after; and the Chiefs beat them by two touchdowns in Week 3. In Week 4, they showed signs of improvement, losing to the Vikings by only five points; the Bengals won by just seven in Week 5, and in Week 6, they got their first win of the season, beating the Jets by three points. On Sunday, the Dolphins and Patriots squared off in an AFC East showdown, and while the Dolphins built a 13-3 lead at the half, the Patriots scored 21 unanswered points to go up 24-13 late in the fourth quarter. Willis connected on an explosive touchdown pass at the 2-minute warning to bring them close, but a failed 2-point conversion and a failed onside kick set the final score at 24-19. picks.headline: Lions vs. Dolphins 5 Qs preview: Is Miami mirroring Detroit’s 2021 culture rebuild?
picks.blurb: Lions vs. Dolphins 5 Qs preview: Is Miami mirroring Detroit’s 2021 culture rebuild? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Porziņģis stepping away Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Dan Campbell guides the Lions through workouts during a spring minicamp. 2022-06-10 Dan Campbell | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Ryan Mathews · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 2:04 PM UTC · 11 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Detroit Lions head to South Beach for a Week 9 interconference matchup against a young, rebuilding Miami Dolphins team. We had the pleasure of connecting with Kevin Nogle, the Managing Editor of Phinsider to give us some insight into this Miami team ahead of Sunday's kickoff. We learned about the local sentiment surrounding head coach Jeff Hafley's foundational reset, how offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik is tailoring the offense to quarterback Malik Willis, and how Ollie Gordon is handling the backfield workload in De'Von Achane's absence—plus what Miami needs to do to keep pace with Detroit's offense. 1. Miami arguably made more changes to their organization than any other team in the NFL this offseason. New head coach, new quarterback, the changing out of long-tenured skill position players—it was a massive overhaul in South Beach. Although the Dolphins are off to a 1-6 start, how much of that was expected from a team that underwent so many changes this offseason? It's early, but do you get the sense that new head coach Jeff Hafley is the right guy for this rebuild? This year is about setting up the franchise for the future, and while losses are never fun, the struggles were expected. This is the league's youngest team, and they are facing a steep learning curve. Miami has 14 rookies on the roster, plus another seven first-year players. This is clearly a reset of the team's foundation, and there will be growing pains. The Dolphins' schedule has also been brutal this year. They started the year against the Las Vegas Raiders, San Francisco 49ers, Kansas City Chiefs, and Minnesota Vikings, not facing a team that had a loss until Week 5 against the Cincinnati Bengals, who were 2-2 coming into that game. Through Week 8, Miami has faced the league's toughest schedule, with a combined opponent winning percentage of .589. The schedule is not an excuse, but with such a young team, it is another variable to consider. Obviously, things can change, but Hafley has instilled confidence in the fanbase so far. The Mike McDaniel era had some fun moments, but it quickly fell apart and the team never adjusted (and McDaniel still does not seem to have made adjustments as the Los Angeles Chargers struggle this year). I think Hafley's focus on making the Dolphins physical, allowing the younger players to gain experience, and the team's ability to make adjustments, learn from mistakes, and continue to fight even in losing situations indicate he is the right guy for this role. Lions fans saw Dan Campbell build a culture out of tough losses back in 2021; that is exactly the phase Hafley and the Dolphins are in right now. 2. From the outside looking in, Malik Willis was dropped into a tough situation given the pieces around him in the offense—and it looks like, predictably, the passing game has struggled so far. The Dolphins rank 26th in passing DVOA and EPA/pass. How has Bobby Slowik tried to tailor this offense to Willis' strengths? What's working, what's not working, and how much of that is related to a new quarterback in a new system versus the lack of talent personnel-wise? I think we are starting to see Willis find some comfort in the offensive system, and he is starting to play better. Despite being a third-round pick in 2022, Willis has played in only 29 career games, starting just 13. He is a league veteran but really has the starting experience of a rookie. At times, he still seems bothered by the speed of the game, but the experience he is getting this year is already making a difference in his play. I think one of the biggest issues we have seen from Willis is a desire to be a pocket passer. He stays in the pocket longer than he should, trying to find the perfect pass rather than taking something shorter or throwing the ball away to avoid a sack. The offensive line is not doing him any favors, but he has taken multiple sacks by running out of bounds instead of throwing the ball away. He seemed to want to avoid using his legs, but has opened up that part of his game in the last couple of weeks. Slowik, like McDaniel before him, has an offensive system built on quarterback accuracy and timing. He uses bootlegs, run-pass options, and play-action passes to get Willis out of the pocket and seeing open receivers. They also seem to be using some half-field concepts, keeping Willis looking in one area and working from deep to shallow rather than having him search the entire field for receivers. The youth on the roster – especially with wide receivers Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell, and Kevin Coleman Jr. – do not always create separation, and drops have also been an issue. When the primary target is not open on time, a young quarterback hesitates, and behind an evolving offensive line, hesitation leads to sacks. That all relates back to the discussion of Miami's reset this year. The potential for talent is on Miami's roster, but they still need to grow individually and together. The coaching staff is clearly working on the balance between youth and system – relying on a more basic system as the players learn. 3. Losing De'Von Achane in the first month of the season felt especially cruel for this offense that was already so limited on difference makers. The Dolphins rank 9th in EPA/rush (-0.03) but rank near the bottom of the league in rush success rate (26th) and rush DVOA (26th), suggesting that their run game is a boom-or-bust attack. Is that a fair assessment of Ollie Gordon's performance this year? The Dolphins also rank 26th in stuffed rate (22.8%) which is the percentage of runs that earn zero or negative yards. Are those stuffed runs more of an indictment of the offensive line or the coaching/play calling? That seems like a fair assessment. Gordon has been a lot of fun to watch as he breaks out this year, but he is a power-back who works extremely well as a change-of-pace option behind Achane. When he finds space, he is able to break it for a big gain, but it really is boom or bust on each run. Part of that is Gordon and his abilities. Part of that is the offensive line finding space to get him free. And part of that is opposing defenses planning to stop the run. Miami has had success this year, averaging 131 rushing yards per game, and they have topped 100 yards in five of seven games, including one game over 150 yards and another over 200 yards. They also have two games with 74 yards rushing each. Boom or bust. The offensive line—especially last week with Kadyn Proctor out with a concussion—still has work to do to come together as a unit. I think play calling is part of it, but not necessarily because the plays are wrong, but rather because the player is wrong. The rushing attack was built for Achane's skill set, complemented by Gordon. Now, it is a Gordon-led unit and some of the designs are clearly meant for Achane's speed over Gordon's power. We have seen that evolve as Slowik has adjusted to Gordon, but there is an obvious difference between the two players and there will likely be a boom or bust aspect to the Dolphins' ground game all season. The outside zone, stretch concepts were designed for Achane's elite sideline-to-sideline track speed. Gordon is a one-cut, downhill runner. The Dolphins have pivoted to more gap and inside-zone looks to match Gordon's style, but until defenses are forced to back out of the box, stops will linger. 4. Hafley brings his decades of experience coaching defense to Miami, and the numbers related to personnel deployment and coverage usage are pretty interesting through eight weeks. Miami lines up in base personnel 51.7% of snaps, second-most in the NFL, and they're utilizing zone coverage 78.8% of the time (10th in the NFL). How much of these numbers overlap with the talent available on the current roster? In other words, does it feel like Hafley's trying to put his players in the best spots to succeed? Numbers suggest the run defense is bordering on being a top-10 unit, but the pass defense might be the worst in the league. Do those numbers tell the whole story? Hafley definitely relies on base defense and he expects his front four to create pressure, rather than relying on the blitz—especially when compared to someone like Brian Flores, a former Dolphins head coach, and his blitz heavy defense. Hafley expects the pressure to come from the front four, allowing him to keep additional players back in coverage or focused on the run. It has been successful—at least as successful as can be expected with the younger players executing on the field. The run defense has been strong for much of the year. There have been mistakes, especially when an edge rusher bites on a play action, chasing the quarterback and failing to set the edge or runs right past the ball carrier, but overall, they are doing well against the run. Of course, I say all of that knowing full well Jahmyr Gibbs is second in the league in rushing and is averaging nearly five-yards-per-carry, so the pressure is on the defense to continue to find success this week. Does the contrast between the pass defense and the run defense tell the entire story? Not necessarily. The heavy zone scheme with the younger defensive backs is designed to prevent explosive, 60+ yard plays. That is allowing for short and intermediate routes to pick apart defenses (especially when Miami struggles to cover tight ends. Good thing the Lions are not bringing a top-tier tight end into this game, right?!?). Add in that Miami has been playing from behind for much of the year, and the short, possession passing game has been highly effective. I do think Hafley is keeping his defensive calls a little more basic than maybe we will see from him in the next few years, allowing the foundation to be set before he starts building off of it. The Dolphins have stressed that they expect to build for the future through the draft and grow the team from within. If they stick to that plan, I think you will see both the offense and defense evolve as the players grow and Miami moves from a roster dominated by rookies to one with veterans hitting their prime supported by key rookies each year. 5. The Dolphins opened as 7-point home underdogs over at FanDuel Sportsbook heading into this Week 9 matchup against the Lions. What's one thing you want to see, what's one thing you need to see, and one thing you're sure you'll see happen in this matchup between the Lions and Dolphins on Sunday afternoon? I want to see the offense be aggressive and take shots downfield. The Lions are allowing 276 yards per game through the air, and they are banged up. Let Willis test them early, get Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell into the game, and use the play-action to create opportunities. The Dolphins need to come into this game feeling like they have to win in a shoot-out. If they are aggressive on offense, maybe they can catch the Lions a little flat-footed at the start. I need to see the Dolphins continue to make adjustments week-to-week, correct mistakes from the last game, and grow as a unit. That will be true throughout this season. away.blurb: "Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time," the team said in a statement. Nov 2 (Reuters) - Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital, the NFL team said on Monday, a day after he was carried off the field with a frightening injury during a game against the Minnesota Vikings. Campbell lay motionless on the ground after levelling a hit on Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter at Ford Field and was taken to hospital after medical staff removed him from the field. The Pro Bowl linebacker, a captain for the team this season, was drafted by the Lions in the first round three years ago and coach Dan Campbell described him as the consummate teammate. "You get voted captain, that says a ton," said coach Campbell. "He earned every bit of that. He's trustworthy, he's dependable, he'd give you the shirt off his back. He's just all heart, man, all effort." (Reporting by Amy Tennery in New YorkEditing by Christian Radnedge)

picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Browns in Week 9 against the Saints - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Porziņģis stepping away Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms 3 Bold predictions for the Browns in Week 9 against the Saints Jeffrey Olson, Browns Wire · Browns Wire Fri, November 6, 2026 at 1:55 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns are looking to keep pace in the playoff race this weekend. They will have to beat the 2-5 New Orleans Saints to do that and hopefully gain some ground in the AFC North. This is a winnable game, and to expect the Browns to win is not a bold opinion. If you want some sort of bold prediction, then we have those too. A forecast that goes beyond that of normal expectations, but also stays in the realm of reality. Here are my three bold predictions for the Browns against the Saints. KC Concepcion rushing score The Saints do not have a good run defense (ranked 29th in rushing yards allowed). I expect the Browns to lean heavily into their running game. This would be especially true if backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders is starting. I expect that Concepcion will be very involved in the passing game. I also think the Browns will look for creative ways to get him touches considering how elusive and explosive he is. Don't be surprised if he finds the end zone on an end-around or a backward pass type play. Judkins goes off I won't go as far as to say that Quinshon Judkins will have his best day of the year because I don't think he outdoes what he did versus the Titans. However, I don't think this game will be way off from that in terms of production. As stated before, the Saints have a bad run defense. It makes sense to take the ball out of the hands of a backup quarterback and run the ball early and often. Look for a 100-yard day and a score from Judkins. Shough-ing turnovers There is no debate that the Browns defense has been their strength this year. They rank 13th in points allowed per game and 13th in total turnovers forced. This pairs with the Browns' advantage, as the Saints are 6th in the NFL in most giveaways. I won't go as far as to predict a turnover fiesta this weekend, but I will predict that Saints Quarterback Tyler Shough has at least two in this game.
