The Browns are currently in third place within the AFC North division, with the team still thinking about a possible playoff run. While the loss to the Steelers was very disappointing for the Browns, the team still has the utmost confidence as it enters the game this week. However, the Browns will likely be playing the game with backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders, with starter Deshaun Watson dealing with a concussion. It remains to be seen if Sanders will be starting the game, but at this point, it's trending toward happening . Sanders did play last season for the Browns, going 3-4 as a starter at the end of the year. As for New Orleans, they will be coming into the game with a record of 2-5 on the season, but the team did have a bye this past week. New Orleans has gone 0-4 at home this year, giving the Browns some extra ammo going into the week. Experts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report predicted how the contest would go this week. Among these picks, only two of the seven chose Cleveland to go on the road to win this week. O'Donnell and Sobleski were the two to choose the Browns to grab the win this week over the Saints. Cleveland's defense has the talent to keep them in this game, but the offense is likely going to have to win it. For the Browns, whoever is under center will be tasked with getting this team back on track. The offense has sputtered over the last few weeks, and this is an area that Cleveland wants to get back going strong. New Orleans can be a sneaky team, even with their lackluster record on the season, with them having beaten the Baltimore Ravens, with a healthy Lamar Jackson at quarterback, and New York Giants this year. The Saints were expected to be better than where they currently are, so the Browns will need to be careful. Kickoff for this game will take place at 10:00 a.m. PT/1:00 p.m. ET at the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans.

at the Caesars Superdome brings together two teams in very different positions, as the Cleveland Browns (5-3) take the field against the New Orleans Saints (2-5). Cleveland is third in the AFC North but just one game behind the first place Steelers. New Orleans has lost four of their last five games and sit last in the NFC South, but they are also only a game out of first as they return from their bye. The Superdome, however, has not been kind to the Saints who are winless in four home games (0-4). Cleveland, however, is a respectable 2-3 on the road this season. Plenty of positives happening with the Browns this season, but last week’s performance is not one of them. The Steelers thumped Cleveland, 27-6, in Pittsburgh. Cleveland was held without a touchdown for the first time this year, lost two fumbles, rushed for only 34 yards and surrendered eight sacks, while the Steelers piled up 200 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Forced to throw for much of the afternoon, Deshaun Watson completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards without an interception and Harold Fannin Jr. caught 10 passes for 154 yards. New Orleans has not played in a couple weeks, but their last game was also a loss to the Steelers, 16-10, in Paris on Oct. 25. The Saints managed only 18 rushing yards and were shut out in the second half, but quarterback Tyler Shough produced an encouraging performance through the air, completing 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards, one touchdown and one interception. It was symptomatic of the season to date: the offense has no balance. Historically, Cleveland leads the all-time series 13-7, but New Orleans has won each of the last three meetings, including the most recent matchup at this same venue on November 17, 2024. That game was tied 14-14 entering the fourth quarter before the Saints exploded for 21 unanswered points to win 35-14. Taysom Hill was the difference-maker, rushing seven times for 138 yards and three touchdowns, including fourth-quarter scoring runs of 33 and 75 yards, while Derek Carr threw for 248 yards and two touchdowns. Jameis Winston threw for 395 yards and two scores for Cleveland, but the Browns failed to turn their yardage into enough points. away.blurb: The Browns will start Sanders, even though Watson has yet to be ruled out for Week 9. He hasn't practiced much this week, and even if he does somehow clear concussion protocol, the Browns will roll with Sanders as the starter for one week. Cleveland could give Sanders the Week 9 and Week 10 start before the team's Week 11 bye, where they could figure out who should be the starting QB for the remainder of the year. away.headline: Cleveland Browns Injury Report Heading Into Week 8
away.blurb: Let's take a look at some of the injuries the Cleveland Browns have dealt with throughout the 2026 NFL season, looking at both sides of the ball and who is out short- and long-term. The Browns will be without Jenkins for their Week 8 game against the Steelers, and he's required to miss at least four games before becoming eligible to return. For Week 8, the Browns are relatively healthy, with only two players listed as questionable: cornerback Myles Harden and safety Daniel Thomas . Harden suffered a hamstring injury during the Browns' Week 7 but returned to the game. He was limited in practice throughout the week and is questionable against Pittsburgh. Thomas was also limited throughout the week with an ankle injury and carries a questionable designation. Howard suffered a concussion during Cleveland's Week 7 win against Tennessee and missed all three practice sessions this week. The Browns initially listed him as questionable on Friday but announced Saturday that he had cleared concussion protocol, which is a big relief considering the strength of Pittsburgh's defensive line. Notable Injuries Throughout the Season The Browns haven't dealt with a ton of significant injuries throughout the season, but their most notable long-term loss is linebacker Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah , who has yet to play a snap this season due to a neck injury. The Browns placed him on the reserve/physically unable to perform (PUP) list in May, and this marks the second straight season he's missed due to the serious neck injury he suffered in October 2024. While Owusu-Koramoah's absence isn't new for the Browns, they also lost guard Teven Jenkins to injured reserve last week with a back injury. The most important news for the Browns this week is that offensive tackle Tytus Howard cleared concussion protocol Saturday and no longer carries an injury designation for Sunday. home.headline: Browns’ Harold Fannin Jr. lands on injury report ahead of Saints matchup
home.blurb: The Bowling Green Falcons product popped up on the Browns' injury report on Thursday with a lower-body issue, though he was able to practice in limited fashion with the team. "Browns TE Harold Fannin Jr. was added to the injury report and limited with a groin injury. A groin injury prematurely ended his rookie season and kept him sidelined for much of the offseason workout program," Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN shared via a social media post on X, formerly Twitter. Browns’ Harold Fannin Jr. lands on injury report ahead of Saints matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Browns’ Harold Fannin Jr. lands on injury report ahead of Saints matchup Rexwell Villas, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Thu, November 5, 2026 at 11:20 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns have some injuries to deal with as the 2026 NFL season reaches its ninth week of action. Among the notable players on the team's injury report ahead of its Week 9 showdown against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome in New Orleans is tight end Harold Fannin Jr. The second-year pro has been arguably the most important weapon downfield for Cleveland this season , but the team is facing the possibility of missing Fannin for the game in the Big Easy. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Hopefully, this is nothing but a bit of maintenance on the part of the Browns, but it is still a reasonable cause for concern that Fannin is on the injury report this close to the matchup versus Tyler Shough and the Saints on the road. Fannin still has a chance to practice in full and remove any doubts about his status for Sunday's game, so his situation is worth monitoring, especially given his importance to the Browns' attack. A third-round pick by the Browns in the 2025 NFL Draft, Fannin is leading the team so far this season with 411 receiving yards to go along with three touchdowns on 35 receptions and 51 targets through eight games. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, the Dolphins stifle Jared Goff and the roaring Lions offense Michael Owens/Getty Images Anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 9 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea. The Baltimore Ravens defense entered Week 9 on a 12-game streak of not allowing a 50-yard play, but they allowed two to the Jacksonville Jaguars in the first half of a 33-10 "Thursday Night Football" home defeat. It's also incredibly stunning that Ravens running back Derrick Henry has run for under 60 yards in four consecutive games. However, he did surpass Pro Football Hall of Famers LaDainian Tomlinson and Jerome Bettis for seventh on the all-time rushing list Thursday night. It's also a good thing Baltimore traded for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett this week because the Ravens have now scored 14 or fewer points in four straight games for the first time in Ravens history. What other shocking events could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 9 menu of games? Let's take a look at five bold predictions. Joe Milton-led Eagles upset first-place Giants The New York Giants (4-2-1) are 3.5-point road favorites at the Philadelphia Eagles (2-6), per DraftKings Sportsbook, marking the first time they are favored over the back-to-back NFC East champs since 2016. It makes sense: The Eagles have lost six in a row, and the Giants have gone three consecutive divisional games without a loss. However, the Eagles will snap their losing streak on Sunday behind new starting quarterback Joe Milton III . Milton, who was Dak Prescott's backup with the Dallas Cowboys since 2025, was scooped up off of the Cowboys' practice squad by Philadelphia. He will take his turn at the wheel of the Eagles' offense after Tanner McKee lost all three of his starts this season. Milton will bring big plays back to Philadelphia's offense. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer has compared Milton's arm strength to that of Brett Favre , whom he coached with the New York Jets in 2008. This preseason, Milton showed significant strides in the accuracy and touch departments in Dallas' three exhibition games in 2026. He completed 29 of his 43 passes (67.4%) for 378 yards, three passing touchdowns and no interceptions for a 118.2 passer rating. Milton will use the lessons he learned from Prescott to emerge victorious over a Giants team Prescott has dominated throughout the course of his career. Vikings sack Bills QB Josh Allen more than five times Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores YOLO defense leads the NFL in the following statistics: Scoring defense (13.3 points per game allowed) Red zone defense (25% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-line defense (37.5% goal-line touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (56.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (4-8) Sack rate (11%) QB pressure rate (46%) Blitz rate (73.6%, the highest by any team in the 21st century) They are bad news for any offense, but especially a Buffalo Bills offensive line that is allowing a 38% quarterback pressure rate, the 11th-highest in the league this season. Bills 2024 NFL MVP quarterback Josh Allen has a propensity for going haywire in primetime against the league's top defenses. In the Week 12 edition of "Thursday Night Football" at the Houston Texans last season, Allen absorbed a career-high eight sacks. Playing on the road in Minnesota on "Monday Night Football" in Week 9 against Flores' ferocious pass rush group could lead to a slightly similar disaster. The Vikings will sack Allen over five times, something that has happened to him just four times in his nine-season NFL career. Cowboys hold the Colts to under 20 points The Cowboys' (3-5) defense hasn't recovered from trading away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers less than a month away from the start of the 2025 season. Dallas has allowed 29 points per game since 2025, making them the second-highest-scoring defense in the entire league. That figure is driven by the Cowboys allowing 20-plus points in 15 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the NFL. However, they will go on the road and hold the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) to under 20 points on Sunday. Indianapolis is fresh off a 42-7 defeat at the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8, and they have scored 10 or fewer points in consecutive games for the first time since 2022. Facing a familiar face in Colts quarterback Daniel Jones , whose 68.7 passer rating is the worst in the league this season, the Cowboys will finally hold a team under 20 points for the first time since Week 11 of the 2025 season. Jets' Braelon Allen goes off against Chiefs New York appeared to suffer a major blow when Jets running back Breece Hall , whom the team extended on a three-year, $43.5 million contract this offseason, went down in Week 3 with a quadriceps injury. However, 2024 fourth-round pick Braelon Allen slid into the Jets starting running back spot and has balled out ever since. Allen's 504 rushing yards in the five games since Hall's injury are the second most in the entire NFL behind only Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving's 548. Despite the 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs allowing the eighth-fewest rushing yards per game (96.3) in the NFL this season, Allen will go off for over 100 once again to become the first Jet with five consecutive games with 100-plus scrimmage yards since running back Thomas Jones in 2008. Dolphins hold Lions QB Jared Goff to under 200 passing yards The Detroit Lions (5-2) are soaring this season, leading the NFL in total offense (395.4 total yards per game) and ranking third in scoring offense (29.0 points per game). Quarterback Jared Goff is at the center of that success. Goff is averaging 280.6 passing yards per game (third in the NFL) with 15 passing touchdowns (tied for fifth in the NFL) and just one interception. Goff is the fourth quarterback to have those numbers through the first seven games of a season, joining Tom Brady (2015 and 2016), Alex Smith (2017) and Patrick Mahomes (2019). Goff is also third in the NFL in EPA per dropback (0.25). However, the Miami Dolphins (1-6) will keep Goff relatively in check by holding him to under 200 yards passing. The only team to do that to Goff in 2026 is the Vikings, the NFL's No. 1 defense. However, the Dolphins will do it on the strength of 2024 first-round edge rusher Chop Robinson's efforts. Robinson leads the NFL in quarterback pressure rate (20.6%) this season (among those with at least 100 pass-rush snaps), and Robinson will get in Goff's face enough to throw him off his game. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brandon Lee Gowton · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 7:19 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Six straight losses for the Philadelphia Eagles. Can the Birds snap the streak against the New York Giants, a division foe they've owned for a long time? In order to preview this Week 9 NFC East matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Big Blue View . The earnest Ed Valentine kindly took the time took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let's take a look at the answers. [For my answers to Ed's questions about the Eagles, stay tuned to BBV .] 1 – The Giants are off to their most encouraging start to a season in a long time. What has John Harbaugh specifically contributed to this team's turnaround? Credibility. That is the first word that comes to mind. He had 15 winning seasons in 18 years in Baltimore, and he didn't have to prove himself to anyone. He has driven the Giants hard and made them believe they have earned the right to win because of what they have done. I think this piece I wrote on Tuesday is instructive. Harbaugh isn't afraid to challenge players or to step on toes to make the Giants better. 2 – J.J. McCarthy's playing time has been limited but he's shown some promise. To what extent is there confidence in him moving forward this season? I don't know that there is confidence. There are, of course, already fans willing to trade Jaxson Dart and run with McCarthy next year. It is way too early for that, though. I think the best word is "excitement." The Giants did not give up on the season when Dart was lost. They went out and traded for McCarthy, which delivered the message they were not throwing in the towel. McCarthy has shown arm talent and mobility in 5 quarters. He gives them more upside than Jameis Winston. His skillset allows them to run the offense the way they designed it for Dart. Can he keep it up? Can he force the Giants into a Dart-McCarthy debate this offseason? I don't know, 3 – Who are the some of the more underrated Giants players this season? Perhaps some for the Eagles to keep an eye out for in this game? That's hard, honestly. Rookie WR Malachi Fields is developing nicely. Bryan Hudson has taken the center job away from John Michael Schmitz. Abdul Carter doesn't have big sack numbers, but he has been hell to block all season. Deonte Banks has been playing well, really well. He looked like a No. 1 shutdown cornerback in Week 7 against Nico Collins of the Texans. 4 – What's the biggest matchup in the Giants' favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? The run defense has been hit and miss. Saquon Barkley hitting the home run still scares me. The Giants are solid against the run, until they aren't. When they aren't, they give up big plays. Other than that, the thing that scares me is that I still think the Eagles defensive front can dominate games. 5 – Who wins this game and why? With the Giants currently listed as 3-point road favorites (first time they've been favored in Philly since 2009), what's your score prediction? With great trepidation, I will pick the Giants to win. I'm still wrapping my head around the Giants being favored. They were 10.5-point underdogs two weeks ago in Houston. They have not won in Philly since 2013, and I am well aware that bad things always seem to happen to the Giants at the Linc. I have said for year, though, that at some point things have to turn around. I think this is the year they finally do. I will say Giants 24, Eagles 17 .

Philadelphia released its final injury report Friday, ruling out DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), Jonathan Jones (hamstring), Britain Covey (knee), and Michael Carter II (abdomen). Backup quarterback Tanner McKee is questionable with a rib injury after being limited in Friday's practice. The injury adds another development to Philadelphia's quarterback situation after head coach Nick Sirianni announced that Joe Milton III would replace McKee as the starter against New York. With Smith and Wicks unavailable, Philadelphia will need increased production from rookie Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, and the remaining healthy receivers. Tight ends Dallas Goedert and Eli Stowers could also play important roles as offensive coordinator Sean Mannion attempts to create manageable passing opportunities for Milton. Covey's absence further limits Philadelphia's receiving depth and removes an option in the return game. Jihaad Campbell, Jonathan Jones and Michael Carter II ruled out The Eagles will also be shorthanded defensively, with Campbell, Jones and Carter II unavailable against a Giants offense led by quarterback J.J. McCarthy. Campbell has been dealing with hamstring and quadriceps injuries, while Jones remains sidelined with a hamstring issue. Carter II has not recovered from an abdomen injury that forced him out of last week's loss to Washington. Saquon Barkley limited, Tanner McKee questionable Barkley was listed as a limited participant Friday because of hamstring and back injuries, but he does not carry a game-day injury designation. His availability matters as Philadelphia tries to establish a more productive rushing attack against his former team. New York enters Week 9 allowing 128.1 rushing yards per game and 4.8 yards per carry. McKee's questionable designation also creates uncertainty behind Milton. The former Stanford quarterback was limited Friday after being listed as a full participant earlier in the week. The Eagles will face the Giants on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at Lincoln Financial Field before entering their Week 10 bye. away.blurb: Here's what to know about Skattebo's injury and when he might return to the field for the division-leading Giants . The Giants are listing Skattebo as "doubtful" to play in the team's Week 9 game against the Eagles. The second-year running back was unable to practice leading up to the game, being listed as a non-participant at all three of New York's sessions. John Harbaugh didn't rule Skattebo out during his media availability following Friday's practice, per ESPN's Jordan Raanan . However, the new designation would suggest Skattebo is unlikely to play, a fact that could be strengthened if the Giants elevate a running back from their practice squad on Saturday. The Giants have not yet provided a definitive timeline for Skattebo's return to the field. The Giants inked Desrosier to their 53-man roster to poach him from the Chargers, so he may get a first crack at backing up Singletary with Skattebo out. The New York Giants are dealing with an injury to their clear-cut top running back coming off their bye week. Cam Skattebo is dealing with a hamstring injury that he suffered on the final carry of his Week 7 game against the Houston Texans. He pulled up lame at the end of a 42-yard run in overtime and ceded the field for the final snap, which resulted in a game-winning, 30-yard Devin Singletary touchdown run. Skattebo didn't seem concerned about his injury after the game, so many believed the second-year running back would be good to go for the team's Week 9 game against the Philadelphia Eagles. From NFL plays to college sports scores, all the top sports news you need to know every day. Instead, Skattebo has continued to be absent from practice, which has thrown his status into flux. Is Cam Skattebo playing Week 9? If Skattebo doesn't play in Week 9, his next chance to suit up will be the Giants' "Thursday Night Football" game against the Washington Commanders in Week 10. Harbaugh didn't seem overly concerned about Skattebo's absence being of the long-term variety. He referred to the running back as "day-to-day" entering the practice week while saying the team would take a wait-and-see approach with the 24-year-old. During a Wednesday, Nov. 4 press conference, Harbaugh also alluded to the tricky nature of predicting recovery for soft-tissue injuries, like hamstring problems. "Skatt's got a hamstring, so you know how that goes," Harbaugh said , referring to Skattebo by his nickname. "We'll see." Devin Singletary is currently entrenched as the clear-cut backup to Skattebo. The 29-year-old veteran is in his third season with the Giants but has played sparingly to date, racking up 80 yards and a touchdown on 18 carries. Singletary produced exactly 437 rushing yards in each of his first two seasons with the Giants while serving largely as a backup or third-string option. home.headline: DeVonta Smith, Saquon Barkley update. Eagles coach defends QB change
home.blurb: PHILADELPHIA − DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks will miss their third straight game as they have been ruled out for the Eagles game against the New York Giants on Nov. 8. As for running back Saquon Barkley, he has been cleared to play. Barkley has been dealing with hamstring and back injuries that have limited his workload for the past two games. It’s expected that Barkley will once again be on a pitch count against the Giants. LB Jihaad Campbell (quad/hamstring) S Michael Carter (abdomen) and PR Britain Covey (knee) were also ruled out. None of them have practiced this week. It should be noted that McKee is listed as questionable with a rib injury. Neither wide receiver practiced this week, including on Nov. 6. Smith has a hamstring injury that has recurred since the summer, while Wicks is dealing with an ankle injury. Buy Philadelphia Eagles tickets The Eagles (2-6) are in the midst of a six-game losing streak, their longest since the 2012 season. And they're changing quarterbacks, going with Joe Milton, whom they signed on Oct. 16 from the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad, in place of Tanner McKee. Milton, a sixth-round pick of the Patriots in 2024, has never started in an NFL game, although he has appeared in five (one with New England in 2024 and four with Dallas last season). Nick Sirianni on why he changed QBs Eagles coach Nick Sirianni explained the decision to go with MIlton on Nov. 6. "It's a difficult thing to think through because it isn't ever just on one person," Sirianni said. "Matter of fact, I think Tanner played solid. But this is just what I felt like we needed to do right at this particular moment to give ourselves the best chance to win this weekend." Sirianni had said on Nov. 2 that "Tanner is our guy" when asked if he was considering switching QBs. On Nov. 4, he made the switch. "You look through the game like we just got off of, and then you're starting to look through the game and the game plan, and as you start to put ideas down, and things are fluid," Sirianni said. "The toughest part about this is I felt Tanner did solid. I thought he did a lot of good things, so that's always tough." When pressed further on why Sirianni didn't mention the QB change during his Nov. 4 press conference, before the news broke that the Eagles were making the change, Sirianni cited competitive advantage and not wanting to reveal the change to the Giants. "I'm going to tell you what I want to tell you guys," Sirianni said. "I respect the job that you all have to do, but I'm going to tell you what I want to tell you guys because I'm always going to protect the team, first and foremost. Every second that goes by in a situation like that, that you can hold onto that information as long as you possibly can, is a little less time for the opponent to get ready for the game." Although the Commanders' 2-4-1 record is far from impressive, they remain a dangerous team that can win on any given Sunday. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn is currently fighting for his job , and injuries have plagued the team throughout a disappointing season. Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has missed several games this season after aggravating a previous arm injury, while several other key players have been sidelined for significant periods of time. While they are 2-4-1, the Commanders still have an opportunity to win the weak NFC East. The Commanders just won their second game of the season after defeating the Philadelphia Eagles and currently sit third in the division. This season, the Commanders are 17th in points per game and 26th in points allowed. They have also struggled on third down, converting just 32% of their attempts, while their defense has surrendered too many points. Although the Commanders have been one of the worst teams this season, they have found success running the ball. Led by their dual-threat quarterback, they average 127 rushing yards per game and protect the ball with only three turnovers. The Commanders' biggest weakness lies in their passing defense, which ranks 27th in the league, allowing 243 yards per game and an opponent passer rating of 100.6. The Rams' success largely depends on quarterback Matthew Stafford's ability to effectively move the ball. Stafford is reportedly dealing with soreness in his right arm. He left the locker room after the Chargers game with a bag of ice on his right elbow. This could be a big game for Puka Nacua . Held to only 80 yards in Week 9, Nacua might have over 100 receiving yards this week. The Rams should still find success running the ball, but the overall game will depend on Stafford's effectiveness passing the ball. In a must-win game for the Rams, this news comes at the worst time. Written by NDTV Sports Desk Updated: November 05, 2026, 7:53 AM EST Read Time: 2 min facebook twitter WhatsApp reddit E-mail Matthew Stafford during an NFL game. © X/@RamsNFL The Los Angeles Rams QB Matthew Stafford walking around with ice wrapped around his throwing elbow raises questions about his health. With the team already dealing with several injuries, losing another player was the last thing they needed. However, Stafford had a rather relaxed response when reporters asked about his condition on Wednesday, November 4. The 38-year-old made it clear that the soreness had not affected his work or his ability to play. Matthew Stafford speaks out on injury concern Stafford did not appear particularly concerned about the attention surrounding his elbow. In fact, he joked that reporters had only recently started noticing something he had been doing throughout the season. "You guys have been blind. I feel like I've been icing my arm every day out here, walking around," the quarterback told reporters. He then explained that some discomfort was understandable at this stage of his career. Stafford, in his 18th NFL season, admitted the physical demands of competing against younger players but insisted that the issue had not stopped him from practicing or taking snaps on game day. "Listen, I'm 38 years old, trying to keep up with these young bucks. Little bit of soreness and stuff that is not uncommon this time of year," he added. His comments gave some relief after head coach Sean McVay had confirmed earlier in the week that Stafford was experiencing soreness in his right arm. The quarterback had been spotted with ice on his elbow after the 24-9 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 8. The first injury report for Week 9 listed Stafford with a right elbow issue, but he remained a full participant in practice. That was another positive sign for a team relying heavily on its veteran quarterback. away.headline: Commanders vs. Rams Friday injury report: Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown out
away.blurb: The Commanders receiver corps is being thinned out by injury. Washington will play Sunday’s game against the L.A. Rams without Treylon Burks or Dyami Brown, the team announced Friday evening on its official injury report. Burks is dealing with a foot injury that kept him out of practice all week. Brown suffered a calf injury in Thursday’s practice that the Commanders are concerned about. Johnny Newton was considered questionable on the injury report, as those on IR with open practice windows usually are. We should learn about his availability on Saturday. TE John Bates – Limited all week with a shoulder injury All this comes shortly after Terry McLaurin was lost for the year with a torn petellar tendon in his knee. As The Athletic’s Nicki Jhabvala originally pointed, Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams were the only receivers at practice who have caught a pass in a game to this point. That’s, well, not great. The injury report was relatively clean outside of that, though the team has absorbed significant recent losses of those — like Javon Kinlaw and Jeremy McNichols — who are now on injured reserve. Also, NFL Network reports that superstar Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett is expected to be activated off injured reserve for Sunday’s game. Here’s the full Commanders injury report: WR Dyami Brown – Suffered calf injury during Thursday’s practice WR Treylon Burks – Suffered foot injury vs 49ers DT Jer’Zhan Newton – 21-day practice window opened; returning from IR (pec) DL Shy Tuttle – Has a shoulder issue from Week 8 G Sam Cosmi – Dealing with a new knee injury, full practice Friday OT Josh Conerly – Dealing with a new finger issue QB Jayden Daniels – Still listed with Week 2 elbow dislocation TE Colson Yankoff – New knee injury What’s your level of concern with the state of the Commanders injury situation? away.headline: Rams-Commanders injury report: Trent McDuffie, 2 other starters questionable
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: That's the good news. The bad news is three other starters are in danger of missing the game, landing questionable tags for Sunday's contest. McVay said before practice that Trent McDuffie, Kam Curl and Colby Parkinson are all questionable to play. McDuffie will not practice, which will be his third straight DNP this week. He injured his back while making a tackle last week against the Chargers and has been held out of practice ever since. Additionally, Jordan Whittington (back) and Grant Stuard (hamstring) will be listed as questionable and will be limited in practice on Friday. Long snapper Joe Cardona is still dealing with an ankle injury and is doubtful to play. That puts Jake McQuaide in line to make his second straight start for the Rams. Update (5:15 p.m. ET): Terrance Ferguson has now been ruled out after injuring his hamstring in practice on Friday. For the Commanders, wide receivers Treylon Burks and Dyami Brown have both been ruled out, leaving Washington thin at the position. Defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton is also questionable, but he practiced all week in full. home.headline: Rams get major Myles Garrett injury news ahead of Commanders game
home.blurb: The Rams could get another massive boost on Sunday too. According to NFL insiders Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport, Myles Garrett is on track to be activated from Injured Reserve ahead of their Week 9 matchup against the Washington Commanders. He returned to practice Wednesday after missing the last seven games, although he remained a limited participant on Thursday. The Rams opened his 21-day practice window earlier this week, giving them an opportunity to activate him once he’s ready. The latest report suggests that could finally happen this weekend. Getting Garrett back would be huge for the Rams, who need another reliable pass rusher next to Byron Young, who already has 4.5 sacks this year. Aaron Donald hasn’t lived up to the hype yet in his return to the NFL, and Kobie Turner remains on IR with a groin injury. We also haven’t truly got to see Garrett and Donald play together yet, giving fans another reason to get excited for Sunday. The Los Angeles Rams have started to find their footing after a difficult opening stretch, winning back-to-back games to improve to 4-4. They first secured a big 35-21 road victory over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7, and then followed that up with a convincing 24-9 win over the Los Angeles Chargers last weekend. They still have more work to do if they want to become genuine Super Bowl contenders, but momentum is starting to build for Sean McVay’s squad. More news : Jaguars’ Liam Coen Moves Ahead of 2 NFL Legends on All-Time Coaching List The Rams traded for Garrett in June, sending Pro Bowl pass rusher Jared Verse and multiple high draft picks to Cleveland in exchange for the two-time Defensive Player of the Year. However, his first game with Los Angeles couldn’t have gone worse. He played 40 defensive snaps in the season opener against San Francisco, but didn’t record a single sack or tackle. Garrett later admitted that his knee was bothering him, and after undergoing surgery, he was placed on IR. More news : Ravens Hit With Harsh John Harbaugh Reality After Jaguars Blowout More news : Eagles’ Dallas Goedert Has Telling Reaction to Joe Milton Starting At 4-4, the Rams might not feel like the Super Bowl favorites they entered the year as, but there’s still time to turn it around. They’re third in the NFC West, behind the 6-1 49ers and 4-4 Seahawks, both of whom they’ll play again later this season. If the Rams can start stacking wins and get healthy by the time those crucial matchups roll around, they can build serious momentum toward the end of the year and into the postseason. After Sunday against the Commanders in Washington, the Rams will face the Cardinals in Arizona before home games against the Packers and Chiefs. Getting Garrett back now could be the spark this team needs to go on a run. home.headline: Myles Garrett Injury Update, Latest on Rams Star's Status vs. Commanders
home.blurb: Los Angeles Rams superstar pass-rusher Myles Garrett is set to return to the lineup against the Washington Commanders on Sunday. The 30-year-old veteran set the single-season NFL sack record in 2025 with 23, and the Rams likely assumed they would get something resembling that level of production out of him. Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters Garrett is expected to play on Sunday after NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported Garrett was "on track to be activated" after practicing all week. Garrett has not played since Week 1, as he underwent arthroscopic knee surgery and was placed on injured reserve following the Rams' season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers. L.A. made the blockbuster trade of the offseason when it acquired Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in exchange for pass-rusher Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, and 2028 second-round pick and a 2029 third-round pick. A seven-time Pro Bowler, five-time First Team All-Pro and two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Garrett was coming off the best season of his career. However, Garrett did not look himself in Week 1 after battling a knee injury during training camp and the preseason, and the decision was made for him to undergo surgery and heal up. Given that the Rams entered the season as the clear Super Bowl favorites, the 2026 campaign has been largely disappointing thus far. Los Angeles has a 4-4 record, placing it third in the NFC West, and it would not be a playoff team if the season ended today. Garrett could give the defense a significant lift if he is fully healthy and back to his usual form, though, which is ideal with winnable games on tap against the Commanders and Arizona Cardinals the next two week. The schedule gets tougher after that with games against the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs and 49ers, and the Rams' likely hope by that point is that Garrett will have knocked off the rust and be positioned to contribute in a major way.

picks.headline: Week 9 Preview: Can the Carolina Panthers Keep Up With the Denver Broncos?
picks.blurb: Week 9 Preview: Can the Carolina Panthers Keep Up With the Denver Broncos? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Porziņģis stepping away Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Week 9 Preview: Can the Carolina Panthers Keep Up With the Denver Broncos? | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Sue Levine, Editor Christopher Mason · Last Word on Sports Fri, November 6, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Carolina Panthers are coming off a mini-bye week following their Thursday night football loss to the Green Bay Packers . Now, they prepare to welcome one of the AFC's top teams, the Denver Broncos . Denver travels to Charlotte following a close win against its division rival, the Kansas City Chiefs. This will be the ninth meeting between the two teams, with the Broncos holding a 7-2 advantage over Carolina, including their victory in Super Bowl 50. The Panthers enter this matchup barely holding on to their first-place lead in the NFC South and riding a two-game losing streak. Meanwhile, the Broncos sit comfortably atop the AFC West and look to extend their lead against a struggling Carolina team. Both teams have their own issues. Carolina's defense has looked like a shell of itself while dealing with injuries and coaching changes. Denver's offense, meanwhile, has struggled to find consistency in the early stages of games, often waiting until the second half to hit its stride. Although the teams' records suggest a mismatch, this game presents an interesting study in how teams start versus how they finish. Green Bay Packers linebacker Ty'ron Hopper (59) is stiff-armed by Carolina Panthers running back Chuba Hubbard (30) on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Packers won the game, 27-19. Tork Mason/Green Bay Press-Gazette Denver's Offense vs. Carolina's Defense The Denver Broncos are very much a second-half team, with their offense becoming more productive as games progress. Denver has generated 1,066 yards of total offense in the first half compared with 1,110 in the second half. The difference becomes more pronounced in the passing game, where the Broncos have recorded seven second-half passing touchdowns compared with just two in the first half. Bo Nix's yards per attempt also increased to 6.6 after halftime. The Panthers cannot afford to let Denver find its rhythm through the air. One way to prevent that is by generating consistent pressure on Nix, who has struggled against opposing blitzes. Carolina has had difficulty getting after the quarterback this season, with injuries taking a toll on its edge-rushing group. If the Panthers can disrupt Nix in the pocket, they could interrupt the rhythm that has allowed Denver to become more productive in the second half. Carolina must also find a way to stop the run. It is a message Coach Dave Canales has emphasized to new defensive coordinator Todd Wash . The Panthers have struggled against opposing rushing attacks, allowing approximately 140 yards per game on the ground. Denver uses its rushing attack to create favorable passing opportunities for Nix by forcing opposing safeties closer to the line of scrimmage. Running back Jonah Coleman also brings the speed to create problems for Carolina's defense at the second level. The Panthers showed some improvement against Green Bay, holding the Packers to fewer than 100 rushing yards while generating penetration from defensive tackles Lee Hunter and Derrick Brown. If Carolina can force Denver's running backs to deal with linebackers Devin Lloyd and Bobby Okereke, the Broncos could have a more difficult time creating the deep passing opportunities Nix prefers. Establishing control of the line of scrimmage will be critical to keeping Denver's offense in check. Oct 18, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Carolina Panthers defensive tackle Lee Hunter (92) and linebacker Bobby Okereke (58) during warmups against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Can Carolina's Secondary Stop Bo Nix? The Carolina Panthers' secondary faces a productive touchdown scorer in Bo Nix. However, the Denver quarterback enters this matchup with some concerning passing efficiency numbers. Nix is averaging 6 yards per attempt while completing approximately 60% of his passes. He has also thrown nine touchdowns against three interceptions. His 83.6 passer rating further highlights some of the inconsistencies in Denver's passing attack. Those numbers present an opportunity for Carolina's secondary to disrupt the Broncos' aerial game. The Panthers will need to force Nix into difficult throws and make him take risks when attempting to push the ball downfield. However, Nix is particularly effective at extending plays and creating open passing lanes with his mobility in the pocket. Carolina's inability to generate a consistent pass rush could work in Denver's favor. If the Panthers cannot pressure Nix, he will have additional time to find receivers Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle downfield. However, if Carolina's secondary can stay with Denver's receivers, Nix may be forced to extend plays and search for alternative passing windows. The Panthers must force Nix into difficult throwing angles and prevent him from creating open passing lanes over the middle of the field. Doing so could limit Denver's explosive plays while disrupting the timing of its offense. The longer Nix has to hold the football while searching for an open receiver, the more opportunities Carolina's defense will have to make a play. Nov 1, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) leaves the field after defeating the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Bryce Young vs. the Broncos' Defense The Carolina Panthers will have their hands full against Denver's defense. The Broncos enter this matchup tied for fourth in the NFL with 23 sacks. Bryce Young was sacked six times last week and has taken 11 sacks over the past two games. Young struggled to recognize pressure against Green Bay, while Carolina's offensive line consistently had difficulty giving him enough time to operate. This week, the Panthers' offensive line will have to contend with Nik Bonitto, Jonathan Cooper, and Zach Allen. All three have been among Denver's leading sack producers this season and have established themselves as key disruptors along the defensive front. Carolina will need to find ways to work around Denver's pass rush. That means incorporating quick passes, getting the football into the hands of its playmakers, and establishing a more consistent rushing attack. The Panthers do not have an elite running game, but Chuba Hubbard has shown the ability to break off explosive runs when given the opportunity. If Carolina can get Hubbard going early, it could open up the passing game, particularly through play-action. Carolina will also need to get creative with its receiver alignments. Tetairoa McMillan will likely see plenty of Denver's premier cornerback, Pat Surtain II. The Panthers should move McMillan around the formation to create more favorable matchups and prevent Denver from consistently deploying Surtain against Carolina's leading receiver. Similarly, if Jalen Coker is healthy enough to play at full strength, Carolina's receiving duo could give Denver some problems. Having multiple receiving threats available would make it more difficult for the Broncos to focus their coverage on McMillan. Ultimately, Young needs to get the football out quickly, avoid unnecessary sacks, and take advantage of the opportunities Denver's defense gives him. Oct 29, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) during the game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images The Last Word The Carolina Panthers will have their hands full against a tough opponent this week. While Carolina is struggling to keep its head above water, last week's game showed glimpses of the team fans had seen earlier in the season. The Panthers made a late push against Green Bay, fighting until the final seconds despite being outplayed for much of the night. If Carolina can keep Nix in check by forcing him to extend plays, disrupting his passing rhythm, and containing Denver's rushing attack, the defense could give the offense more opportunities to compete. On the offensive side of the ball, offensive coordinator Brad Idzik needs to return to some of the principles that made Carolina's offense successful earlier in the season. Establishing the run will go a long way toward opening up opportunities for the receivers while giving Young more time to make the throws he needs. If Carolina can execute complementary football and Todd Wash's defense shows signs of improvement under its new leadership, the Panthers could make this a competitive matchup. However, beating Denver will require four quarters of consistent football. Carolina cannot afford another slow start or a second-half collapse. Against a team that has made a habit of getting better as games progress, the Panthers will need to put together their most complete performance in weeks. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 injury report: S Brandon Jones trending toward inactive
away.blurb: Denver Broncos starting safety Brandon Jones was among three players who missed practice for a second consecutive day and now appear highly questionable to play in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last week's victory over the Chiefs and has yet to resume practicing. Ditto for defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, whose shoulder issue has held him out. Ditto for cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, who's dealing with an ankle affliction. Each player will need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up at Carolina. In more fortunate news, Denver's other starting safety, Talanoa Hufanga, was upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) to a limited participant on Thursday, giving him a shot at returning after being sidelined for the last three games with his own ankle malady. WRs Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Pat Bryant (ankle) were full participants, as well. Bryant will return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury. On Carolina's side, five players did not practice: OLBs Jaelan Phillips and Trevis Gipson, CB Will Lee, OG Damien Lewis, and LB Bobby Okereke. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was a full participant and will play against the Broncos. Assuming Jones is ruled out, Taylor Rapp would likely fill in as a starting safety at Carolina. If Hufanga can't go, Devon Key or JL Skinner would slot in next to Rapp. Skinner, in particular, had a standout game in last week's comeback victory over the Chiefs . Assuming Abrams-Draine is out of commission, second-year CB Jahdae Barron could see an uptick in snaps behind CBs Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian. Wide receiver Courtland Sutton and defensive end Zach Allen were also upgraded to full following a veteran rest day on Wednesday. Both will be active in Week 9. “You’ve definitely seen his ascension, and he’s very comfortable with what they’re doing," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Young on Wednesday. "It’s an explosive team. I think they’re seventh or eighth in explosives. They do a great job mixing the play action, the ‘RPO’ (Run-Pass Option) game. They’ve drafted well. So all those numbers are different today than they were two years ago.” Assuming Uwazurike is scratched, Sai'vion Jones would likely be penciled in as a starting DE opposite Allen, with third-round rookie DL Tyler Onyedim a possibility to make his NFL debut. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 Injury Report: Final Decisions on Jones, Uwazurike
away.blurb: The Denver Broncos released their final Week 9 injury report on Friday -- and in doing so, ruled out a trio of defensive players, including two starters. Neither of the players got in so much as a limited practice this week -- three consecutive DNPs -- so the writing was on the wall for defensive coordinator Vance Joseph's esteemed unit. Also on that side of the ball, the Broncos listed safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) and outside linebacker Dondrea Tillman (hip) as questionable to play at Carolina. Hufanga has missed the last three games due to his injury, while Tillman popped up on the injury report Friday despite a full practice. Elsewhere, wide receiver Pat Bryant is questionable for a Week 9 return following a four-game absence with his own ankle issue. Denver designated Bryant to return from injured reserve and he's expected to be activated to the 53-man roster. The Panthers, meanwhile, ruled out four starters including cornerback Will Lee, linebacker Bobby Okereke, outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips, and left guard Damien Lewis. The good news as it relates to Jones' absence is that it appears to be aligning with the return of Hufanga, and Denver demonstrated that on Friday by releasing fill-in starting S Taylor Rapp, presumably signaling that Hufanga will play in Week 9. Look for Devon Key and/or JL Skinner to also see an uptick in snaps. Among those inactive against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday will be safety Brandon Jones, defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, and cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, all of whom suffered injuries during the team's Week 8 win over Kansas City. Per The Denver Gazette's Chris Tomasson , "it's very uncertain" as to whether Tillman, who's classified as "week to week," will see the field at Bank of America Stadium. Perhaps he's given some time off ahead of next week's bye. Defensive end Zach Allen, receiver Courtland Sutton, and receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) were given no designation and are good to go versus Carolina . How the Broncos Overcome Defensive Losses Second-year corner will take Abrams-Draine's reps as the No. 4 CB behind Pat Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian. It's possible the Broncos promote one of their three defensive backs, Sean Fresch Jr., Brent Austin, or Ugo Amadi to help provide some depth. With Uwazurike sidelined, the onus will fall more on DE Sai'vion Jones opposite Zach Allen, though it's also likely that third-round rookie Tyler Onyedim, a weekly healthy scratch, finally makes his NFL debut. If Tillman can't go, Que Robinson could assume the lion's share of reps as the No. 3 OLB behind Nik Bonitto and Jonathon Cooper. Los Angeles is the only team in the NFL without a win and are as a result, firmly entrenched in the cellar in the AFC West. Houston sits in second in the AFC South but are three games behind the first place Jaguars. The Texans take the field following their bye week. They were last in action on October 25 when they lost a disappointing 27-21game in overtime at home to the New York Giants. Houston rallied from a seven-point fourth-quarter deficit to force overtime on C.J. Stroud’s 3-yard touchdown pass to Xavier Hutchinson with 52 seconds remaining. Stroud finished 17-of-28 for a season-low 153 yards and two touchdowns, while Woody Marks ran 19 times for 66 yards, but Houston produced only 237 total yards. The glaring issue was on defense. The Texans surrendered a season-high 188 rushing yards, including 124 and a touchdown to Cam Skattebo . The Chargers’ search for their first victory continues following their most recent game, a 24-9 loss last Sunday to the Rams. The Chargers had a 9-3 lead late in the first half but went scoreless over the final 38 minutes of the game. Justin Herbert completed 24 of 32 passes for 257 yards, but threw two interceptions, and the Chargers failed to reach the end zone for the second consecutive game. Los Angeles managed just 64 yards rushing with all nine Chargers’ points coming on Cameron Dicker field goals. The Chargers hold a narrow 6-5 advantage in the all-time series, but Houston has won the last two meetings, including two especially consequential victories. The Texans routed Los Angeles 32-12 in the AFC Wild Card round following the 2024 season, intercepting Herbert four times as Houston erased an early 6-0 deficit and ran away with the game. Houston then went back to SoFi Stadium in Week 17 last season and beat the Chargers 20-16, giving the Texans consecutive victories in the series for the first time. The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-7 after falling to the Los Angeles Rams on the road in Week 8. Now the Chargers will have a chance to face off against the Houston Texans at home in Week 9. The Texans have found their fair share of struggles this season at 2-5, but they are fresh off of their annual bye and are well-rested for the matchup. The Bolts entered this week as 4.5-point underdogs, per FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under is currently set at 41.5 points. The Chargers struggled once again when facing the Rams. The Chargers had a 9-3 lead with 2 minutes to go in the second quarter, but they proceeded to give up a touchdown drive to close out the first half, which gave the Rams the lead going into the locker room. From there, the Rams capitalized and scored twice more in the third quarter to take a 24-9 lead, which ended up being the final score. Hope is not lost for the Chargers as they hold on to the No. 1 overall pick for the 2027 NFL Draft. However, getting a win or two would give them some morale for the second half of the season. Perhaps this will be the week the Chargers will have a chance to get their first win. When the Los Angeles Chargers landed in Week 9, hosting the Texans at SoFi Stadium, I think most fans and media looked at that matchup as one of the most even matchups on the board, a game that could go either way. Nine weeks into the season, anyone who thought that is, in actuality, correct, but I doubt that anyone who viewed this game as an even matchups back in September figured it would be even because both teams stink. After all, these are two teams who reached the postseason the last two seasons. Instead, both teams are a combined 2-12. In short, these are two bad, underachieving squads. Make no mistake, this is a bigger game for the Texans than it is for the Chargers. The Chargers’ season is essentially over. They’re more worried about making sure their quarterback, who makes $55 million per year, isn’t broken, than they are worried about out the postseason. The Texans still harbor faint playoff hopes, and losing to a winless, rudderless mess like the Chargers would take the low point of the DeMeco Ryans Era, which is where we are right now, and plunge it into the center of the earth. This is a must-win for the Texans, flat out. Here are four things to watch for this weekend in this game: 4. What exactly got fixed during the bye week? As Coach Ryans pointed out in multiple media appearances over the last two weeks, there were no shortage of areas to reassess and focus on improvement. The Texans have been among the worst tackling teams in football, and probably not coincidentally, they did what Will Anderson described as “pee wee ball” tackling drills on Wednesday. The Texans have been among the most penalized teams in football. I’m not sure how a bye week fixes that, but it needs fixing. Communication on defense has been a major culprit in the Texans’ allowing the highest number of explosive plays in the NFL. This also must get fixed. Finally, play selection and play calling have been inconsistent and flat out bizarre at times. Ryans indicated they had meetings to address that, as well. The proof will be in the play on Sunday. 3. Tank Dell and Marvin Harrison, Jr. During the bye week, the Texans placed wide receiver Jaylin Noel on injured reserve with a toe injury. He is done for the year. Fortunately, Tank Dell returned just before the bye week, and with some noticeable overlap in skill set with Noel, Dell is likely ready to assume some of Noel’s workload. Additionally, Harrison, the Texans’ big trade acquisition in October, has played just a few snaps in each of his first two games as a Texan. That needs to change, especially if the Texans are looking to recoup the value of the second round pick they sent to Arizona in exchange for Harrison. Finally, Nico Collins needs to flat out be on the field more than he was against the Giants, where he played barely 60 percent of the snaps. This wide receiver room has talent, and it’s up to OC Nick Caley to deploy it, and stop running these “jumbo” packages with six offensive linemen. 2. Justin Herbert’s slow meltdown into football hell If you listen to my radio show, you know that I’ve long felt that Herbert has been one of the most overrated entities in the NFL. Despite never winning anything of substance, including a single playoff game, so called “experts” have insisted on placing Herbert among the top half dozen or so quarterbacks in the NFL. With Mike McDaniel hired as the OC in Los Angeles, this was supposed to be the season where Herbert’s game actually elevated to the level people have insisted he’s played at since arriving in 2020. Instead, Herbert has been arguably the worst quarterback in the league, throwing ten picks in seven games, and being the steward of an offense that hasn’t scored a touchdown in 27 straight possessions. I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t enjoying Herbert’s meltdown validating my opinion of him as a player. I’d also be lying if I said I wasn’t terrified that his breakout game is going to happen this weekend against the beleaguered Texans defense. 1. C.J. Stroud’s run to (contractual) glory, continued Thankfully, the Texans clearly have the better quarterback in this matchup, and likely in every matchup in the schedule the remainder of the season. Despite the team’s 2-5 record, Stroud has been outstanding this season, as he is among the league leaders in passing yards, and has thrown 11 touchdowns to just one interception. The Chargers are 0-7, but their defense has been their strong suit this season. If the Texans are going to make a run at a playoff spot in the second half of the season, unless the defense recaptures its magic of 2025, they will likely need Stroud to keep playing at an elite level, and if he plays at that level for another ten games, he is going to get paid a LOT of money this offseason. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Imagn Images It's safe to say that last week lived up to the hype. The Detroit Lions defeated the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings , the Denver Broncos used a goal-line stand to hand Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs their second consecutive loss, and the Chicago Bears upset the Seahawks in Seattle with some help from trade-deadline addition Jeffery Simmons . This weekend in the NFL , the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons will battle in Madrid, Jordan Love takes the Green Bay Packers to Foxborough to play the New England Patriots and Baker Mayfield gets a shot at Caleb Williams and the red-hot Bears. Which teams should you pick in Week 9, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 4 from DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research for its hard work. Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens (TNF) Dajani ( Jaguars -10): It's tough to pick this game since we are unaware of the Baltimore Ravens ' quarterback situation. Will they be starting rookie third-stringer Joe Fagnano , or someone else? I believe the Jaguars will win, but any team can cover a double-digit spread at home. Jacksonville is a remarkable 14-3 over its last 17 games and is the only NFL team leading its division by three or more games. Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in passer rating (112.6), while the Jags lead the league in points per game differential (+12.1). Sure, you can say the Ravens will just ride Derrick Henry , but the Jaguars have what is statistically the No. 1 run defense in the NFL, and have gone 24 straight games without allowing a 75-yard rusher. … Prediction: Jaguars 28, Ravens 13 Dubin (Jaguars -10): The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. … Prediction: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) vs. Atlanta Falcons (Madrid) Dajani (Falcons +3): I may take the upset here. I'm aware the Falcons just registered one of the most embarrassing losses of the season in Tampa, but I'm willing to overlook that given how bad the weather was. I have some questions about the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner has a heel injury, and Cashius Howell just broke his wrist. Then, this Cincy defense allowed the lowly Tennessee Titans to put up 440 yards of total offense last week and allowed the first Titans' 300-yard passing game since the 2023 season. Tony Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns, so what is Bijan Robinson going to do? Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best wide receiving duo in the league, but the Bengals may be due for their first loss in over a month. Remember, this Falcons team beat the San Francisco 49ers the last time they played a game indoors. Give me the points. … Prediction: Falcons 27, Bengals 23 Dubin (Bengals -3): The Cincinnati offense is rolling, with Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dunking on opposing defenses. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been struggling to run the ball as of late despite the presence of Bijan Robinson (48 carries for 200 scoreless yards in the last three weeks). The Bengals do provide an opportunity for the run game to get back on track (4.8 yards per carry allowed), but Dexter Lawrence has shut down other rushing attacks before. If the Bengals can keep Robinson in check, I'm not sure Atlanta can count on Michael Penix Jr . to go shot for shot with Burrow. … Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 20 Los Angeles Rams (-5.5) at Washington Commanders Dajani ( Rams -5.5): I think the Washington Commanders are a feisty team that could cover this number, but don't forget that this is somewhat of a revenge game for Sean McVay. He spent seven seasons in Washington before the Rams made the smart decision to hire this 30-year-old kid to run their franchise. In his first season as a head coach, McVay lost to his former team. Since then, he's 2-0 vs. Washington, winning each game by at least eight points. The Rams are coming off back-to-back wins by 14+ points. They also could get Myles Garrett back on Sunday. LA is 11-2 SU and 10-3 ATS in its last 13 games vs. teams entering below .500. … Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 17 Dubin (Rams -5.5): The Rams have finally climbed back to .500 with back-to-back wins over the Raiders and Chargers , and I think they can keep things rolling here by doing what they did against those two teams: running the ball. Washington has actually been pretty good against the ground game this year, but it just lost Daron Payne to a significant injury. On the other side of the ball, I don't think we can count on the Commanders' offense to produce enough points to keep up with LA's offense. … Prediction: Rams 24, Commanders 16 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Dajani (Broncos -2.5): I told you the Broncos would beat the Chiefs last week. The conversation around Bo Nix is so bizarre to me. He's not Josh Allen , obviously, but he's not worth benching either. He's not the most prolific passer in NFL history, but he's Superman when it comes to leading his team to wins in crunch time. Denver does have a great defense, which pulled off that goal-line stand vs. Kansas City, but Nix leads the NFL since 2000 with 9.1 yards per attempt when down by one score in the fourth quarter. He has 15 game-winning drives to his name, which is one shy of the most in a three-season span in NFL history. Nix hasn't even played three full seasons. It hasn't always been pretty, but Nix is pretty good in those fourth quarters. This week, Denver travels to take on the Carolina Panthers . Bryce Young 's offensive line has some serious issues, and those were evident last week against the Packers. Through Week 8, Carolina has allowed 23 sacks, which is tied for second-most in the NFL, with 11 of those sacks coming in the past two games. Plus, the Panthers' defense has allowed an incredible 42.7 points per contest in their first three home games, which eventually led to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero last week. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Panthers 20 Dubin (Broncos -2.5): I'm not buying into Nix as much as Dajani is, but I am buying into Denver's defense being able to get after Bryce Young behind what is an increasingly leaky offensive line and preventing the Panthers from denting the scoreboard. If they can keep this a low-scoring game, I like them to pull out a win on the road. … Prediction: Broncos 23, Panthers 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (-3) Dajani (Packers +3): The Packers got some extra rest following their Thursday win over Carolina, while the New England Patriots couldn't run away from the Miami Dolphins . This Packers offense has been fun to watch — not counting the ground game, which has registered the fewest rushing yards (485) by a team above .500 through eight games in NFL history. However, Jordan Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards, while Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first duo to have 600 yards receiving each through eight games since Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill in 2022! Drake Maye has been great, having scored at least three touchdowns over five straight games, but this Packers defense will provide quite the test. Green Bay has allowed just 14.6 points per game over its last five. … Prediction: Packers 27, Patriots 24 Dubin (Packers +3): I also think Green Bay's extra rest will matter here, even if only because it will give Christian Watson some extra time to heal up from the ribs injury he suffered last Thursday night. The Packers are going to need him against New England, even if he ends up drawing shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez , as that will just open things up for Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft . Meanwhile, Green Bay's defense has been excellent for several weeks now, and with the Patriots down multiple weapons in the passing game, I think the Packers can try to make New England one-dimensional here, limiting their chances to move the ball downfield. … Prediction: Packers 26, Patriots 20 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears (-6) (SNF) Dajani (Bears -6): I correctly chose Chicago to cover in Seattle last week, and I became even more confident in that pick when the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons. The Seahawks' addition of Quenton Nelson is a great one, but I think the addition of Simmons is even better. He's the best defensive tackle in the NFL and makes life incredibly difficult for quarterbacks. In his first game for his new team, he recorded six tackles, one sack and two tackles for loss. Chicago's defense allowed just 3.0 yards per play with him

Yours truly correctly predicted the Chicago Bears to take down the Seattle Seahawks on Monday Night Football. We move on to Week 9 and we're hoping for more upsets during this weekend's action. Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 9 Upset Pick Minnesota Vikings (+150) vs. Buffalo Bills Josh Allen has a history of struggling against defenses as aggressive as the one Brian Flores operates. Allen did finally get by the Texans in Week 1, but that defense has drastically regressed this season. The Vikings’ defense has formed into what many expected to see out of the Texans in 2026. Minnesota is No. 1 in points allowed (13.3) and No. 2 in total defense (271.6). Yes, I do worry about Minnesota’s poor offense, but maybe Kyler Murray turns it around against the Bills’ poor defense, which is allowing 25.9 points per game. This will come down to Allen against the Vikings’ vaunted defense. Peter Dewey Week 9 Upset Pick Green Bay Packers (+140) vs. New England Patriots The Green Bay Packers can’t run the ball this season, averaging just 2.9 yards per carry, but that may not matter on the road against the New England Patriots in Week 9. New England is 20th in the league in EPA/Pass and eighth in EPA/Rush on defense, so the Packers and Jordan Love are likely going to lean on their elite passing game on Sunday. The Pack are coming off a mini-bye after playing on Thursday against Carolina, and they’ve won four of their last five games after a 1-2 start. Meanwhile, New England is extremely banged up at receiver and was in a dogfight against the lowly Miami Dolphins in Week 8 before pulling away in the second half. The Pats have struggled a bit against elite competition this season, losing to Seattle, Jacksonville, and Chicago. Will we see a similar result against Green Bay? The Packers are quietly fifth in the NFL in EPA/Play on defense, and Love has been playing at a high level all season long. There aren’t a ton of great upset spots this week, but Green Bay’s recent form is intriguing against a banged-up New England squad. Iain MacMillan Week 9 Upset Pick Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+240) vs. Chicago Bears You can win a lot of games in the National Football League if you can run the ball effectively and play elite defense, and that's exactly what the Buccaneers have been doing. In fact, they shut the Falcons out last week without completing a single pass. They now enter this week ranked inside the top seven in every rushing metric, second in opponent EPA per play, and third in opponent success rate. We don't currently know what sort of form Baker Mayfield is in, but if he's in peak form when the Bucs need him to take to the air, Tampa Bay is going to be an extremely dangerous team. I have little bad to say about the Bears, who have proven me wrong about my preseason evaluation of them. New England didn't play the prettiest game on the field, but at this point for them, a win is a win. With all the injuries that the Patriots have seen take place, especially to the offense, the team has been able to stay alive. This week, the Patriots will be hosting the Green Bay Packers, giving the team a real challenge on its hands. Green Bay, like New England, has started to play much better of late, finally put things together on the field. The Packers will be entering the game with a record of 5-3, with both sides of the ball clicking for the team. New England is going to have to be careful in this game; otherwise, they could be on the losing end of the contest. Analysts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report all made picks for the game between the two teams. But six of the seven experts went with Green Bay to take down the Patriots in this matchup. Only Gagnon went with New England to win the game, despite this contest being played at home for the Patriots. But the Packers recent play likely has to do with how confident those around the league are heading into the week. One key for New England this week will be how quarterback Drake Maye performs, especially when it comes to turnovers. The Green Bay defense can be feisty at times, using its opportunistic nature to get the best of opposing quarterbacks. Maye will have to find a way to overcome the injuries that the Patriots have seen this year, going against this tough defense. But the veteran quarterback has done well this year , even with his issues earlier in the season. Against Green Bay, the Patriots may need to rely on the running game a little more, taking some pressure off Maye's shoulders. Head coach Mike Vrabel will have to put his signal-caller into a strong position to win, avoiding any issues. The offensive line will also need to hold up in the game, giving Maye time to throw the ball against this defensive front. Kickoff for the Patriots game against the Packers is scheduled to take place at 1:25 p.m. PT/4:25 p.m. ET at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough.
