picks.headline: Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9
picks.blurb: Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Porziņģis stepping away Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:49 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This is one of the most interesting and compelling games of the schedule for Week 9 and the first half of the NFL season. The Green Bay Packers are starting to find their offensive rhythm with Jordan Love improving on a week-by-week basis, but the team is still waiting for Micah Parsons to return to help the defense assert itself. The New England Patriots are in full stride at the moment. After losing two of their first three games and looking like last year's Super Bowl champions might take a step or two backwards, the Patriots have found their stride once again. It certainly begins with Drake Maye , who is starting to make a case as one of the NFL's elite quarterbacks, but it goes much deeper than that. The Patriots have been getting excellent play from their offensive line and running back Rhamondre Stevenson is one of the most dependable players that head coach Mike Vrabel has on his roster. His presence is a security blanket to the rest of the team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) While the Patriots are feeling better about themselves on an every-week basis, the defense is also getting the job done. New England ranks 9th in scoring defense , as the Patriots are giving up 20.3 points per game. However, the Packers may be encouraged when they look at the New England pass defense because that unit is only slightly better than average, ranking 13th in the league. Jordan Love will throw for 250 yards and 2 touchdowns The Packers would like to come at the Patriots with a balanced, versatile and unpredictable attack. The return of Josh Jacobs from the commissioner's exempt list gave head coach Matt LaFleur a solid option running the ball. However, recent allegations of additional domestic violence incidents against Jacobs could result in additional discipline by the NFL. While he is still eligible at this moment, LaFleur might want to bypass that portion of the gameplan. As a result, it will be on Love to direct a consistent offensive attack, and he will be under significant pressure from the Patriots' aggressive defense. Love is one of the best pure passers in the game, and if the offensive line gives him protection, he can drive the Green Bay attack. Love has completed 192 of 312 passes for 2,246 yards and is averaging 280.8 yards per game. He has thrown 16 TD passes and 6 interceptions. He has a trio of receivers who are likely to cause problems in Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and TE Tucker Kraft. Watson's speed, route running and dependable hands should help the Patriots stay in this vital road game. Look for Love to connect with Watson for at least one key touchdown in the fourth quarter. Maye will approach 225 passing yards and 2 touchdowns Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Look for Maye to be turned on to the maximum level for this matchup with Love. He knows that Love throws one of the best deep balls in the league, and Maye wants to compete with him in all areas. While Love is also a good runner who can escape the pass rush, Maye excels in that area. Look for Maye to show off those running skill early in the game, and that will force the Packers to employ a spy who will attempt to contain the quarterback. That's when Maye will start to show off his pinpoint passing. The Patriots quarterback has completed 157 of 234 passes for 1,983 yards with 15 touchdowns and 8 interceptions. In addition to those numbers, his confidence is sky high. While the Patriots have not gotten the production from former Eagles wideout A.J. Brown, he can depend on wide receiver DeMario Douglas and tight end Hunter Henry to show off their productivity against Green Bay's eighth-ranked pass defense. Stevenson will rush for 75-plus yards and 1 TD The Patriots have one of the most underrated running backs in the game in Rhamondre Stevenson. While he is not a gamebreaker in terms of speed, he understands all aspects of the game. He runs well between the tackles and he will finish off his rushing attempts with power. He knows how to set up his blockers and accelerate at the right moment. The Patriots have TreVeyon Henderson — when healthy — to show off his skills as a speed back. However, it is Stevenson who is a difference maker and will give the Patriots the edge they need to beat a solid opponent. Patriots will outlast Packers and earn 27-24 triumph The escape factor that Maye provides will allow him to buy extra time and create more plays for the Patriots. This will allow them to maintain possession and sustain their drives. He will also get a huge lift from Stevenson, who is simply a winner and will come through when the game is on the line. The Packers will push the Patriots to the limit, but the Pats will have the benefit of their homefield, as well as their two key difference makers. New England comes away with this exciting and well-played victory. home.headline: Patriots get bad AJ Brown injury news ahead of Packers game
home.blurb: Now, it looks like Drake Maye will be without his No. 1 receiver once again, with head coach Mike Vrabel officially ruling Brown out for Sunday’s game against the Green Bay Packers. The fact that he’s been ruled out Sunday against the Packers isn’t entirely surprising given that he missed every practice this week. But it adds to Brown’s frustrating first season with the Patriots, and now there are even growing concerns about the condition of his knee, with some questioning how much longer he can truly keep playing at an elite level. As for Brown’s return, there’s no set timeline. He could be back next week against the Detroit Lions, which will be played in Munich, Germany, but with a Week 11 bye, the Patriots might also choose to play it safe and hold him out for that game as well. A.J. Brown went down with an ankle injury in the New England Patriots ‘ season-opening loss to the Seattle Seahawks nearly two months ago. An MRI later confirmed it was a high ankle sprain, and the team placed him on Injured Reserve soon after, costing him the next four games. His Patriots debut ended with just three catches on four targets for 26 yards. Brown returned against the New York Jets in Week 6, but finished that game with three catches on 10 targets for a mere 27 yards, and then hauled in three catches for 48 yards the following week against the Chicago Bears. But he missed last week’s win over the Miami Dolphins with a knee issue and didn’t participate in practice all week. More news : Rams Get Major Myles Garrett Injury News Ahead of Commanders Game The latest report means Brown will now have missed six of nine games in his first season in New England. That’s not what Patriots fans were expecting when the team traded a first-round pick (and a fifth-rounder) to get him, or for a player making $32 million per year. Even in the three games he’s appeared in this year, Brown has been outplayed by the likes of Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, and Hunter Henry. More news : Patriots Get Concerning News as TreVeyon Henderson Reveals Health Scare More news : Jaguars’ Liam Coen Moves Ahead of 2 NFL Legends on All-Time Coaching List Without Brown, Maye will need to keep spreading the ball around. Douglas is New England’s leading receiver on the year with 26 catches for 332 yards and four touchdowns, followed by Henry with 29 catches for 326 yards and two touchdowns. Efton Chism III has also stepped up recently, hauling in a team-high five catches for 37 yards in last week’s win over the Dolphins. Those receivers should all have important roles against Green Bay. It's the old Battle of the Bay against their former rival San Francisco 49ers. It should be a good game. Here are the picks by the Raiders Wire staff. Game picks for Raiders Week 9 matchup vs 49ers Justin Melo -- 49ers 30, Raiders 24 The Las Vegas Raiders will encounter a San Francisco 49ers offense that is firing on all cylinders right now. There's no reason to believe this struggling defense will match up nicely with Kyle Shanahan's unit. Lamarr Fields -- 49ers 34, Raiders 23 The 49ers run the ball well and Raiders can't stop the run. Also the 49ers defensive front is good and will cause problems for the Raiders. Las Vegas will compete tough but San Franciso will pull away late. Marvin Uzor -- 49ers 31, Raiders 24 Cousins and Bowers keep it closer than people think through the air. But a run defense giving up 5.1 yards a carry against a rested Shanahan team coming off a bye is asking for trouble. Raiders cover, Niners win. Levi Damien -- 49ers 30, Raiders 20 Five straight games the Raiders have given up at least 30 points. The two worst instances were against good teams that had a bunch of injuries that looked like they would struggle to put up points. Those games were the Patriots and Rams . And in both cases, the Raiders defenese got shellacked. They even gave up 33 points to the Jets. So, I don't see any real difference here, even with the 49ers set to be without top receiver Mike Evans and possible two other key receivers as well. The difference here is the 49ers defense is better, so I see the Raiders stumbling in this one. picks.blurb: Raiders vs. 49ers bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Porziņģis stepping away Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Raiders vs. 49ers bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:56 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Las Vegas Raiders arrive at Levi's Stadium with renewed confidence. The San Francisco 49ers arrive with extra rest and something to prove. Las Vegas snapped a four-game losing streak with a 38–33 victory over the Jets, improving to 4–4. San Francisco, meanwhile, returns from its bye at 6–1 after suffering its first defeat, a 29–20 loss to Atlanta. Their November 8 matchup offers a test of whether the Raiders' rebound represents progress or another temporary escape. The opening market favors San Francisco by 10 points, with a total of 51.5. These predictions envision something more explosive than that total suggests: a quarterback showcase, a monster receiving performance and a decisive fourth-quarter separation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brock Purdy throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Purdy will deliver his most convincing statistical statement of the season, reaching 350 passing yards and throwing four touchdown passes. That projection starts with a favorable matchup. Las Vegas has surrendered at least 30 points in five consecutive games, allowing opponents to dictate too many possessions. Even Sunday's victory required the Raiders to overcome 33 points from the Jets. Purdy already has 1,748 passing yards and 15 touchdowns through seven games. Before the bye, he threw for 288 yards against Atlanta despite injuries affecting several important offensive contributors. The Raiders should expect Kyle Shanahan to test their coverage communication immediately. Motion, play-action and layered routes can create uncertainty without requiring Purdy to hold the ball for extended periods. My projection anticipates San Francisco attacking through the air even after establishing a lead. Rather than leaning exclusively on clock management, Shanahan will keep exploiting favorable matchups. Brock Bowers produces 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns The Raiders' best answer will come through Brock Bowers, who will turn a difficult road assignment into a dominant individual performance. The prediction is at least 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns, including one reception covering 40 or more yards. That would require Las Vegas to build its passing plan around Bowers rather than waiting for him to emerge naturally within the progression. Quick throws would establish his involvement, while crossing routes and seam opportunities would provide the bigger gains. Kirk Cousins enters the matchup following a three-touchdown performance against the Jets, and his recent play has kept rookie Fernando Mendoza on the sideline. That continuity matters for this prediction. The Raiders can attack with an experienced quarterback rather than simplifying everything around a developmental transition. The projected game script should also create volume. If San Francisco scores early, Las Vegas will need to maintain an aggressive passing approach rather than protect field position. Bowers would become the central answer, particularly on third downs and near the goal line. His production will keep the Raiders competitive longer than expected, even as their defense struggles to match it. The teams combine for 70 points as San Francisco wins 42–28 The final prediction is a shootout that eventually becomes a comfortable 49ers victory. A 42–28 result would produce 70 total points, sailing past the opening 51.5-point total while giving San Francisco a 14-point winning margin. The logic connects the first two bold predictions, Purdy repeatedly punishes defensive breakdowns, while Cousins and Bowers generate enough offense to prevent an early rout. Ultimately, the difference will be possession-to-possession consistency. Las Vegas will manufacture explosive moments, but San Francisco will sustain more scoring drives and turn one late Raiders mistake into the decisive touchdown. The Raiders will show offensive resilience. The 49ers will show why their ceiling remains substantially higher. The Niners are big favorites in a game that's expected to be high-scoring. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , San Francisco opened up as 9.5-point favorites with the total set at 51.5. That ties for the highest total this season and the second-largest point spread. Raiders games have been video game-esque. They just beat the Jets 38-33. They let the Rams score 35 in Week 7. The Bills scored 33 in Week 6, and Drake Maye dropped 45 the week prior. Geno Smith threw for 290 yards. Adonai Mitchell was unguardable, while Garrett Wilson had a "quiet" 83 yards. It was a different story against the Rams. Kyren Williams and Blake Corum each ran for over 90 yards. Let's just say the 49ers aren't going up against the 2000 Ravens. Klint Kubiak has the Raiders' offense functioning. Ashton Jeanty was not the lead back against the Jets. Instead, rookie Mike Washington got the carries, with 25 compared to Jeanty's two. That offense runs through Brock Bowers, who had 10 targets against the Jets. Bowers finished with seven catches for 92 yards and two touchdowns. Kirk Cousins, who threw three touchdowns, has no problem tossing it up to Bowers in contested situations. Bowers has double-digit targets in all but two games this season. He's a monster, so you understand why Vegas goes out of their way to feature him. The 49ers haven't covered the spread in a couple of weeks. They've also gone under the total in back-to-back weeks. For a while there, it felt like this would be a dead-on over team. Will things change this week?

Instead, he and his agent, Drew Rosenhaus pulled up outside of the team offices. Despite not taking questions, Rosenhaus released a statement, with Aiyuk adding his own take, as captured by The Post . Brandon Aiyuk and his agent Drew Rosenhaus have arrived at the 49ers’ offices. We'll keep that between us and the Niners. Obviously we are here with all of the right intentions.” The team had previously stated that he has played his last down for San Francisco. The enigmatic wide receiver then provided a brief statement. “I am feeling grateful and healthy through a long recovery process, rehab process. I am back to 100% and looking to re-extended into the National Football League.” The veteran wide receiver suffered a serious knee injury that required multiligament surgery. According to a report by NFL Insider Tom Pelissero, Aiyuk owes the 49ers approximately $13 million in bonus forfeiture. The 49ers paid Brandon Aiyuk a $23 million signing bonus in 2024 and a $22.9 million option bonus in 2025, which totals $45.9 million. Aiyuk officially left the team about three-fourths of the way through the 2025 season, thus a 28% bonus forfeiture is owed. Niners general manager has not minced words when expressing his thoughts toward the wideout. Neither has head coach Kyle Shanahan, who offered just four words on Friday. Amidst all of the controversy swirls yet another story. Aiyuk has an outstanding warrant for his arrest for a reckless driving charge. Police were seen outside of the stadium on Friday morning on multiple occasions. This is a developing story with more to follow. picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for Seahawks vs. Cardinals in Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Porziņģis stepping away Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Story by Seattle Seahawks On SI articles 3 Bold Predictions for Seahawks vs. Cardinals in Week 9 Seattle Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Randy Gurzi · Seattle Seahawks On SI articles Fri, November 6, 2026 at 6:30 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Seattle Seahawks have an opportunity to get back on track this weekend as they host the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9 . Seattle suffered a frustrating loss last Monday night against the Chicago Bears, dropping them to 4-4 on the season. Arizona, on the other hand, improved to 3-5 on the season after knocking off the Dallas Cowboys. They're going to be full of confidence, but Seattle will as well. Despite Sam Darnold suffering a quad injury, the Seahawks know they can win this one after backup Drew Lock led them to a 31-7 win over the Cardinals in Week 2. Seattle needs this win to stay in the race for a spot in the NFC playoffs. Securing that win becomes far more likely if the following three bold predictions come true. Zach Charbonnet runs for his first TD of the season Seattle Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet carries the ball against the Chicago Bears. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Zach Charbonnet made his season debut in Week 8. He made it back quickly from a torn ACL suffered in January, but was still shaking off the rust against Chicago. Charbonnet had 23 yards on just six carries and added six yards on three receptions. His workload should increase each week as he gets more comfortable on the surgically-repaired knee. In this bold prediction, he turns the extra touches into his first trip into the end zone of the season. Seahawks record five sacks Seattle Seahawks defensive tackle Byron Murphy II against the Arizona Cardinals. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect During the first meeting, the Seahawks held Jacoby Brissett to just 95 yards passing and sacked him twice. Brissett was traded to the Baltimore Ravens after losing the starting spot to Gardner Minshew, who will have his hands full with the Dark Side defense. In our second bold prediction, that defense, led by Byron Murphy, sacks Minshew a total of five times. Jalen Milroe makes his first appearance of the season Seattle Seahawks quarterback Jalen Milroe drops back to pass against the Kansas City Chiefs. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If the 31-7 win in Week 2 is any indication, the Seahawks should be able to win this one easily. Sure, they will have far more confidence following the performance of Minshew and Tyler Allgeier in Week 8, as they led a 14-point comeback in the fourth quarter. That said, this defense is far more imposing than what Minshew faced in Week 8 against the Dallas Cowboys. picks.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals are coming off a thrilling 33-30 overtime comeback win over the Dallas Cowboys on the road in Week 8. They have made a change at quarterback, benching Jacoby Brissett in favor of Gardner Minshew, who orchestrated the fourth-quarter comeback. Now they face the Seattle Seahawks in Week 9, their second meeting of the year, this time in Seattle. The Cardinals are, as one would expect, huge underdogs. Let's look at the betting odds and lines for this Week 9 matchup. Odds come from BetMGM Sportsbook. Cardinals at Seahawks Week 9 betting odds, lines Cardinals +475 Seahawks -625 The Cardinals are 3-5 after their 33-30 overtime win over the Dallas Cowboys. The Seahawks lost on Monday night 34-17 to the Chicago Bears . The Seahawks beat the Cardinals 31-7 in Week 2 in Arizona. With these odds, the Seahawks are considered about 69% more likely to win the game than the Cardinals. Cardinals +11 (-108) Seahawks -11 (-110) The Cardinals are the biggest underdogs of the week. The 11-point spread is the largest of the week. The Cardinals are 4-4 ATS this season. The Seahawks are 3-5 ATS. For a Seahawks ATS bet to cash, they have to win by at least 12 points. If the Cardinals win, tie or lose by 10 or fewer points, a Cardinals ATS bet wins. Over 44.5 (-108) Under 44.5 (-110) The Over wins if the two teams combine for at least 45 points. The Under cashes with 44 or fewer combined points. The total in their first matchup was 38. Five of the Cardinals' last six games have had totals above 44. Four of the Seahawks' last six games have as well. The Cardinals and Seahawks kick off from Lumen Field on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET (2:25 p.m. Arizona time). home.headline: Seahawks' final Week 9 injury report paints a downright miserable picture
home.blurb: Nelson is out after having a "minor" procedure on his knee, one that the team claims the left guard had before he was traded by Indianapolis. The other players missing read like a who's-who of Pro Bowlers. Seahawks' Mike Macdonald rules Sam Darnold out for Week 9 vs. Cardinals The Seattle Seahawks seem snake-bitten in 2026. For example, the recently acquired Quenton Nelson hadn't missed a game since 2021 before being dealt from the Indianapolis Colts to Seattle. He will now miss his second potential game with the Seahawks with a knee issue. Nelson isn't the only key player missing as head coach Mike Macdonald's team prepares to face the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9. Arizona hasn't defeated the Seahawks since 2021. That could change this week. Seattle Seahawks' Week 9 final injury report is ugly Leonard Williams, Uchenna Nwosu, Charles Cross, Sam Darnold, Rashid Shaheed, and backup nose guard Brandon Pili will also miss the game. In terms of final weekly injury reports, Week 9 is as ugly as it gets for the Seahawks. The players who will miss the game might be too much to overcome even against the Cardinals. In fact, the Seahawks seem to be a diminishing squad that is trending toward missing the playoffs. Almost all the losses in Week 9 are brutal. The team won't have its starting quarterback, its new left guard, its best defensive lineman, its left tackle, arguably its most well-rounded edge rusher, and its best kick and punt returner. If Seattle were facing a team like the San Francisco 49ers or the Chicago Bears again, Mike Macdonald's team would rightfully be expected to lose by at least two touchdowns. Against a motivated Cardinals team that is smelling blood and having its best chance to beat Seattle in a half-decade, they might win by 10 points. A 4-5 record is not only a realistic possibility for the Seattle Seahawks, but an expectation. Seattle faces an improved Las Vegas Raiders team in Week 10, and then comes the bye week. Seattle could easily be 4-6 by the time it returns to play. Forget the playoffs and the trade deadline . There could be no saving this team. Looking ahead to 2027 is probably the only thing to do. Roster changes could be inevitable, and a change of offensive coordinator could be, too. If the Seahawks defeat the Cardinals, one of the worst organizations in the NFL, with such a banged-up roster, a miracle will have happened. At least there is always next year, 12s. An NFL analyst doesn't see Sam Darnold's absence as a detriment to the Seattle Seahawks. Darnold will miss Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals with a quad injury, and the defending champions will instead turn to Drew Lock for the Week 9 division showdown. Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Ben DiNucci wondered if that switch will actually help Seattle's offense. "I hate to say this: Drew Lock might give the Seahawks a better chance to win at the quarterback position," DiNucci said on CBS Sports' Just Football. Darnold has struggled a year after leading the Seahawks to a Super Bowl title. The 29-year-old has thrown nine interceptions in seven games, with his quarterback rating dipping from 99.1 to 79.5. Meanwhile, Lock led Seattle to a season-opening comeback win off the bench before excelling in a road victory over Arizona. DiNucci suggested that another strong showing against the NFC West opponent could create a quarterback controversy. "Sam Darnold has not played well this year. For whatever reason, he's turning the ball over. This offense looks stuck in the mud," DiNucci said. "I don't want to say this is a soft benching, but Drew Lock -- when he came in relief Week 1 against the New England Patriots -- led that team back. Played really well. High completion percentage, no turnovers. And then Week 2, followed it up against the same Arizona Cardinals team he's gonna play this [week] with 235 yards and three touchdowns. "I'm very intrigued to see what Drew Lock does this weekend. If he plays like he played the first two weeks of the season. I think this is gonna be a very interesting topic the rest of the season."

Baker Mayfield and the Bucs won in Week 8 without completing a pass, and after an 0-4 start they’ve won three of their last four games to put themselves right back in the mix to win a terrible NFC South. The Bucs have back-to-back division wins over Carolina and Atlanta, but things will be a lot tougher on the road against the Bears and an MVP candidate in Williams . Chicago has not lost a game that Williams has started and finished this season (4-0), and it upset the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night in Week 8. The Bears have also scored at least 30 points in every game that Williams has completed this season, making them one of the most dangerous offenses in the league. Oddsmakers have set Chicago as a six-point favorite at home as it looks to get to 7-2 before a Week 10 bye. The Bears are still behind the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings – who beat them earlier this season – in the NFC North standings. Let’s take a look at the opening odds for this primetime matchup in a loaded Week 9. Buccaneers vs. Bears Odds, Spread and Total for NFL Week 9 Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Bucs +6 (-112) Bears -6 (-108) 46.5 (Over -112/Under -108) There hasn’t been any real movement in the odds for this game since they opened on Sunday night, even with the Bears picking up an upset win over Seattle. This is a battle between two very different teams, as Tampa Bay has relied heavily on the running game and its defense to get back in the playoff mix while the Bears are one of the best offenses in football. Chicago ranks 10th in EPA/Play, 11th in success rate and tied for 13th in yards per play this season despite the fact that Williams has missed three full games and part of the team’s Week 2 loss to Minnesota. When the former No. 1 overall pick has been on the field, Ben Johnson’s club has been humming on the offensive end, dropping 34 points in Week 8 against a Seattle defense that is No. 1 in the NFL in success rate and entered Week 8 at No. 1 in yards per play allowed. Tampa Bay’s defense is now No. 1 in EPA/Play after picking off Michael Penix Jr. several times in a rain-soaked matchup in Week 8, but things won’t be nearly as easy against Williams. On the bright side for the Bucs, they should be able to run the ball (eighth in EPA/Rush this season) against a Bears defense that is allowing 4.4 yards per carry in 2026. Chicago traded for star defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons ahead of Week 8, but the Tampa Bay running game – led by Bucky Irving – won’t be easy to stop on Sunday night. I lean with the Bears to win this game, and it’ll be interesting to see if the odds move at all with both teams trending in the right direction with the halfway point of the 2026 season upon us. picks.blurb: Buccaneers vs. Bears bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Porziņģis stepping away Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Buccaneers vs. Bears bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 6:02 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Chicago Bears meet on Sunday Night Football with very different momentum and very different identities. Tampa Bay just beat Atlanta 16–0 without completing a pass. Chicago comes in off an upset of Seattle. The Bears are 6-point favorites, and the total is 46.5. The Bucs have won three of their last four after an 0–4 start, so they are still in the NFC South race. These predictions lean on the contrast between Tampa Bay's run-first plan and Chicago's explosive offense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Caleb Williams leads the Bears past 30 points again Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Chicago will score at least 30 points, and Williams will account for three touchdowns. The Bears have scored 30 or more in every game Williams has finished this season, and they have not lost one he has started and finished (4–0). Since he returned from his hamstring injury, they have not trailed in any of three games. Williams threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns in a 30–24 win over New England. Chicago's pass offense averages 236.4 yards a game compared with 131.4 for Tampa Bay. That edge in the air is the core of this call. Tampa Bay's pass defense gives up 205.9 yards a game, which leaves room for chunk plays. Chicago's offense ranks 10th in EPA per play despite Williams missing three full games. I expect him to throw for at least 275 yards and add a rushing score. The one wrinkle is the Bears' backfield. Running back Kyle Monangai is listed as out with a thumb injury, which could shift more of the offense to Williams. Tampa Bay runs for 200 yards and still loses The Bucs will pile up another 200 rushing yards, and it still won't be enough. Against Atlanta, Tampa Bay ran 56 times for 324 yards. Bucky Irving gained 170 yards on 27 carries, and Kenny Gainwell added 140 on 25. Baker Mayfield attempted only three passes in steady rain. Chicago's run defense is beatable, allowing 4.4 yards per carry. Tampa Bay ranks eighth in EPA per rush, so the ground game will work on Sunday night. The problem is what happens when Chicago scores early. The Bucs average 22.3 points a game. A team rated poorly through the air can't easily come back against the best third-down defense in football, according to one projection. I'm projecting 200 rushing yards because the Bears' run defense can't stop everything. But Tampa Bay's offense needs scoring drives, not just yards, and the run game alone won't produce 30 points. Injuries make it harder. Gainwell is questionable with a hip issue, and outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was trending toward out. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka was inactive last week with a foot injury and is also a concern. Mayfield throws 35 passes and the Bears win 34–20 The game ends with Chicago winning 34–20, and Mayfield forced into a very different afternoon than the one in Tampa. A 34–20 final would add up to 54 points, clearing the 46.5 total comfortably, and it would give Chicago a 14-point cover. Mayfield returned from a fractured thumb two games ago and is still working back to full rhythm. He has 679 passing yards and three touchdowns on the season, so asking him to throw 35 times is a real shift for this offense. That volume creates risk. If Chicago leads by two scores in the third quarter, Tampa Bay has to abandon the run and put the ball in Mayfield's hands. I expect two interceptions, including one that sets up a Chicago touchdown. The Bucs will compete. They'll move the ball, their kicker has been perfect this season and their defense will make a few plays. But the Bears' offense is more dangerous, and they are better built to play with a lead. picks.headline: Week 9 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Bears have momentum going into Sunday night vs. Buccaneers
picks.blurb: Week 9 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Bears have momentum going into Sunday night vs. Buccaneers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Porziņģis stepping away Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Frank Schwab Senior writer Fri, November 6, 2026 at 11:01 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Chicago Bears hype is about to get very loud. This NFL season seems wide open. There isn't one great team yet and there are few trustworthy contenders who have emerged. The Bears seemingly saw it the same way when they traded two first-round picks for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. And through one game, it seems like a transformative trade. The Bears had a fantastic performance on a national stage, shutting down the Seahawks in a 34-17 win . Chicago's Super Bowl odds took a leap, as did Caleb Williams' MVP odds. In a season dying for a dominant team to emerge, maybe it's Chicago. The Bears' offense isn't a question. It has scored 30 points in every game Williams has started and finished (it did score just three points against the Vikings and Williams played three-and-a-half quarters, but that says something about Minnesota's defense). If Simmons has as big of an impact on the defense as it appeared on Monday night, Chicago will be looking really good. Nobody paying attention to the NFL hadn't seen how dominant Simmons is, but it was still impressive to see how quickly he fit in and made plays. Chicago gets another close-up in prime time this week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night. Surprisingly, the Buccaneers are far better analytically than their 3-5 record would suggest. They're fifth in DVOA , eight spots ahead of the Bears, and eight in net EPA (expected points added) per play. The Bears are strong in net EPA, coming in third. The Buccaneers will be completely overshadowed in this game. The Bears will be the focus on Sunday night as they've emerged as one of the NFL's most dangerous teams. That's a reason they're a healthy 6.5-point favorite. That's a lot of points, and the Buccaneers might be secretly pretty good. That's why Buccaneers +6.5 is the pick. And if the Bears blow out Tampa Bay in a big prime-time window, they'll take over as the talk of the NFL, if they're not already. The Bears are 4-0 in games that Caleb Williams started and finished this season. Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 9 of the NFL season: Bengals (-3) over Falcons The Bengals and Falcons go to Madrid, Spain, for this one. The Falcons are nearly impossible to figure out. They followed up a win over the undefeated 49ers by losing to a Buccaneers team that didn't complete a pass. That sums up Atlanta's season. We should trust Joe Burrow, who is on a heater, though there are more questions about Cincinnati's defense after it gave up 36 points to the Titans at home last week. Giants (-3) over Eagles Maybe Joe Milton III gives Philadelphia a boost and the Eagles get their first win since Week 2. But since Jalen Hurts went on IR, the Eagles have lost all three games by double digits. It's not a good team in any way, and Milton is far from a sure thing. The Giants are off a bye and should be feeling good coming into this one. Panthers (+2.5) over Broncos The Broncos are the better team. A few things work against them in this spot: It's an early start on the East Coast, and the Panthers have three days rest advantage. The Broncos are also coming off an emotional win over the Chiefs and there could be a letdown. Denver has been much better at home this season. Carolina has faded after a good start but this is a decent opportunity for a win. Dolphins (+7) over Lions Give Miami credit for playing hard. Maybe at some point that effort starts to fade, but the last time they truly got blown out was Week 2. They lost by 14 points to the Chiefs, but Kansas City led by only seven points with three minutes left. It's possible the Lions score enough to cover, but remember that they're usually a different team outdoors. Chiefs (-10) over Jets Kansas City will enjoy the breather after facing the Seattle and Denver defenses on the road the past two weeks. This seems like the type of game in which the Chiefs could take out their frustrations on an opponent that does have some talent but has won only once since Week 1. Saints (-3) over Browns The Browns are likely going with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback because Deshaun Watson was put in concussion protocol. It's not like Watson was playing so well he's irreplaceable, but Sanders has thrown only three passes all season. The Saints are well rested coming off a bye. The Saints are not a great team this season, but this might be a spot for them to get right. Rams (-5.5) over Commanders Is it time to trust the Rams? They have covered two games in a row without a sweat. Those wins came against mediocre (Raiders) or bad (Chargers) teams, but they did handle business. And the Commanders are mediocre at best and maybe just bad. Let's see if the Rams are truly back. Cowboys (-5.5) over Colts It is incredibly hard to trust the Cowboys, especially as a road favorite. But what we saw from the Colts last week in a 42-7 loss was troubling. There was no fight left in that team, which has lost key players to trades and knows its season is done. This could be a bad mistake, trusting a defense that can't stop anyone to cover almost a touchdown on the road. Taking the Colts at this point is even harder. Texans (-4.5) over Chargers It's a lot for Houston to be favored by this much on the road, however, home-field advantage has been mostly eliminated this NFL season and the Chargers have no home-field advantage — even if that was still a thing. Houston is coming off a bye and still has hopes to revive its season. The Texans still have a 34.4% chance to make the playoffs according to DVOA. The Chargers are 0.0% on that list. They'll cover a spread at some point but it's hard to anticipate when it happens. Raiders (+10) over 49ers The Raiders have four losses, and they came against four of the better teams in the NFL: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills and Rams. The bad news is this week they get the Super Bowl favorites. The 49ers should be getting many players back after their bye. But the Raiders can move the ball and they're getting a lot of points. Seahawks (-8.5) over Cardinals With all the quarterback chaos this week, we get two teams that had a different quarterback in Week 8. Brissett was benched and traded, and Gardner Minshew II takes over. Sam Darnold has a quad injury and he'll be out, with Drew Lock taking over. Lock is a reasonable replacement, and Minshew isn't facing the Cowboys defense this week. Packers (+3) over Patriots The Patriots have a lot of injuries and the Packers have a few days of extra rest. In a game that seems evenly matched, the small edges add up. Green Bay started the season very slow but has looked much better over the last four games, winning three and barely losing at Detroit. New England has also emerged after an early-season slump to win four of five. This is a really fun matchup, and even enough to feel OK taking the points. Vikings (+3.5) over Bills This is an interesting game because the teams have opposite strengths. The Bills have a great offense and bad defense, and the Vikings have a bad offense and great defense. The Minnesota defense held the Bears to three points after all; Chicago has scored 30 points in every other Caleb Williams start. It will be a great test against Josh Allen, who is having another fantastic season. It's never enjoyable to be going against Allen, but getting 3.5 points with a defense this good seems right … as long as the offense does at least a little bit. Mandatory Credit: Jonathan Dyer-Imagn Images Evan Winter, Kole Noble · AtoZ Sports Fri, November 6, 2026 at 4:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Tampa Bay's defense has rattled four straight quarterbacks, and now it heads to Soldier Field to face a 6-2 Bears team with Caleb Williams playing at a completely different level. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers head north to Soldier Field for a Sunday night showdown with the Chicago Bears in Week 9, and it's easily the biggest test of their season so far. The Bears are 6-2, quarterback Caleb Williams is playing lights out, and Chicago just added Jeffery Simmons to the middle of its defensive line. The Buccaneers sit at 3-5, but this feels like a much bigger game than the records suggest. It's also the last game before Tampa Bay's bye week, so a win or a loss could go a long way in shaping how the rest of the season plays out. A to Z Sports' Bears writer Kole Noble joined me to break down the matchup, and there's plenty to unpack. Jeffery Simmons and Caleb Williams have Chicago rolling Bears general manager Ryan Poles sent two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick to land Simmons, and the return showed up right away. Simmons led the entire defensive line in snaps in his debut against the Seahawks on Monday night, recording a sack and multiple tackles for a loss. Seattle averaged about three yards per play with Simmons on the field compared to roughly 13 yards with him off of it. Simmons can truly elevate a defense to another level. He's a power player with quickness, and that creates an automatic matchup to watch against a Buccaneers interior that has struggled with power players. Then there's Williams. The former No. 1 overall pick is completing over 70% of his passes, and over the last three weeks he ranks third in the NFL at 73.8%, behind only Joe Burrow and Matthew Stafford. The Bears are also second in the league in yards after catch in games Williams plays. In other words: he's doing exactly what Bears coach Ben Johnson wants. "I saw Albert Breer say he's more Clark Kent right now than Superman," Noble said. "But when they need Superman, we can still see that." Williams showed it in Seattle, escaping a sure sack and firing a strike over the middle to Rome Odunze. That's going to matter against a Buccaneers defense that has rattled the last four quarterbacks it has faced. It took Aaron Rodgers 17 straight passes and an extra quarter to figure things out. Bryce Young and the Panthers didn't run a viable play in Buccaneers territory until midway through the third quarter. Then the Falcons went 0-for-12 on third down. The blueprint for slowing Williams is simple: speed up the clock, take away his first read, and get pressure quickly. Brian Flores did that in Week 2, throwing disguised looks and blitz packages at Williams, and Chicago couldn't get anything going. The Bears have rarely taken deep shots this year, which could make forcing those throws a smart strategy for Tampa Bay. Where the Buccaneers can attack the Bears Chicago's run game is the backbone of Johnson's offense, but it hasn't been hitting the explosive plays he wants. D'Andre Swift scored three touchdowns last week, though he has rarely broken free for those 10- or 12-yard carries. Kyle Monangai is still dealing with a turf toe injury, and Johnson said he didn't want to put him on injured reserve. The expectation is the Bears will rest Monangai this week and use the bye to get him back for Week 11 against the Saints. That's a good thing for the Buccaneers, whose front seven has been on point against the run all year. The one concern is missed tackles from Alex Anzalone and Josiah Trotter, although most of those have come against the pass. The bigger opportunity is in Chicago's secondary, which has struggled all year long. Outside corners Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson both rank in the bottom 20 in PFF coverage grade, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba gave them fits Monday night. Rookie fourth-round pick Malik Muhammad has been the better option, but he missed last week with a toe injury. That matters even more because Emeka Egbuka logged a full practice on Thursday, which has him on track to play. Tampa Bay shouldn't feel like it ha s to throw the ball. However, if there's a week for Baker Mayfield and the passing game to take their shots, this is it. Final score prediction Kole: The primetime spotlight keeps Chicago from falling into a trap game, especially with Simmons making his Soldier Field debut. picks.blurb: Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Porziņģis stepping away Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Two 6-1 teams enter Monday Night Football with very different questions. Can the Buffalo Bills keep rolling against the NFL's stingiest defense? Can the Minnesota Vikings generate enough offense to avoid wasting another strong defensive performance? Buffalo visits U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9 following a 36–10 victory over Baltimore. Minnesota returns home after Detroit ended its unbeaten start with a 19–15 win. The Bills opened as three-point favorites, setting up a compelling clash between offensive firepower and defensive disruption. These three predictions anticipate a departure from Minnesota's usual defensive script, explosive passing, costly mistakes and a dramatic finish that hands Buffalo its second defeat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Justin Jefferson explodes for 175 yards and two touchdowns Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Jefferson will deliver the performance Minnesota has been waiting for, finishing with at least 175 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Jefferson caught five passes for 33 yards and a touchdown against Detroit and enters Week 9 without a 100-yard receiving game. Buffalo presents an opportunity to change that. Its defense ranks 30th against the pass, making this a matchup Minnesota should attack rather than approach conservatively. The Vikings need to manufacture touches before asking Jefferson to win difficult downfield assignments. Motion, condensed formations and crossing routes would help create cleaner releases and give the quarterback defined throwing windows. The bigger gains should follow when Buffalo adjusts to those shorter completions. One double move or broken coverage could turn a productive evening into a spectacular one. Quarterback availability remains important. Kyler Murray is managing hamstring tightness , with Carson Wentz the likely alternative if Murray cannot play. Expect Minnesota to make its best receiver the centerpiece, not merely a name opponents must account for. Josh Allen accounts for four touchdowns but commits three turnovers Allen will produce enough spectacular plays to keep Buffalo dangerous and enough mistakes to give Minnesota control of the outcome. The bold prediction is four total touchdowns alongside three turnovers, including at least two interceptions. https://twitter.com/search?q=josh%20allen&src=typed_query&f=top Minnesota's defense provides the foundation for that aggressive forecast. Entering Week 9, the Vikings lead the league in points allowed per game at 13.3, quarterback pressure rate at 45.8 percent and sack percentage at 10.96 percent. Pressure alone will not neutralize Allen. His ability to escape the pocket can turn a successful blitz into a defensive emergency, particularly when coverage players must chase receivers across the field. That creates the central tension. Minnesota will win several snaps decisively, but Allen will punish a few failed pressure attempts with explosive completions or scrambling opportunities. The turnovers will come when he tries to rescue plays that should end with a throwaway. Disguised coverage behind an apparent blitz can invite exactly that kind of aggressive decision. Buffalo's offensive line also bears watching. Right tackle Spencer Brown's availability is a concern entering the matchup, potentially complicating protection against Minnesota's pressure packages. Allen will remain the game's most dangerous improviser. On this night, improvisation will carry a substantial price. Minnesota wins 38–35 on a last-second field goal The final bold prediction ties those individual performances together: Minnesota wins a shootout with a field goal as time expires. A 38–35 result would produce 73 points, comfortably exceeding the opening total of 46.5. It would also represent a dramatic departure from the Vikings' defensive scoring average. The logic is not that Minnesota suddenly becomes a bad defense. Turnovers and explosive plays can produce points without requiring long, methodical drives. Jefferson's breakout keeps the Vikings moving, while Allen repeatedly answers before one late mistake gives Minnesota the deciding possession. After losing its unbeaten record, Minnesota will respond with its most convincing offensive statement and a victory that reinforces its place among the league's contenders. picks.headline: Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills
picks.blurb: Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Porziņģis stepping away Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills (Gregory Fisher-USA TODAY Sports) Joey Hickey · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings (6-1) have a pivotal matchup on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. And while losing the game wouldn't make them a pretender, winning the game could solidify the Vikings as contenders. Minnesota has played great defense through seven games, but the offense has been lacking. Now, fans are looking for the team to show improvement on offense. If it doesn't happen, we could see the team explore changes on offense. Vikings Wire's Andrew Harbaugh predicts that Vikings backup quarterback Carson Wentz will see playing time in Monday night's game against the Buffalo Bills. Here's some of what Harbaugh had to say about his chances to take the field for Minnesota in the game. "Kyler Murray has played poorly enough this season and has not shown a real grasp of the offense or the players' tendencies within it. Carson Wentz has not been a rockstar, but he has been more than serviceable for the Vikings when he has played. I predict that the first half could be rough for the Vikings' offense, and at halftime Kevin O'Connell tries to give the offense a spark with a quarterback change." Harbaugh adds that it could be a breakout day for another Vikings player. He has star Vikings wideout Justin Jefferson catching two touchdown passes in the matchup. Here's what he had to say on the breakout. "Justin Jefferson has started to be a bit more vocal about how he feels about the offense being so quiet. I think they make it a point to get him going early in the game, and then by the end of the night he has two touchdowns. They have to get him involved more; the offense goes as Justin Jefferson goes, after all. If they do not use him more soon, then ideas and outside voices are going to start getting louder." Jefferson's frustrations have drawn questions about the player throwing him the football. It's not surprising that there have been questions given all the pieces that the Vikings have on offense. It's not that starting quarterback Kyler Murray has been awful. The offense has been awful, though. Some believe a change at quarterback is necessary to bring a spark. Maybe a change at quarterback isn't the fix, but something will need to change for the offense to start moving the football. If it doesn't the Vikings will have squandered what could be one of the NFL's best defenses of the last decade. We'll keep a close eye on what moves head coach Kevin O'Connell makes when the matchup gets underway with Buffalo.

picks.headline: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Heading Into Monday Night's Matchup With Bills in Week 9
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Heading Into Monday Night's Matchup With Bills in Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Porziņģis stepping away Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms A potentially huge game for Justin Jefferson tops the biggest Vikings bold predictions heading into Week 9's contest against the Bills. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jason Harmon · Minnesota Vikings On SI Fri, November 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It may be hard to believe, but we're already in Week 9 of the NFL season, as your 6-1 Vikings prepare for a matchup every fan had circled on their schedule. The Vikings will host the 6-1 Bills in a Monday night matchup four years in the making. The teams last faced off in an all-time classic in Buffalo in 2022, with Minnesota winning 33-30 in overtime. Expecting the same level of cinematic excitement on Monday night may lead to disappointment, but there's reason to think this game could still be great, especially if the Vikings' offense improves . Let's dive into my boldest predictions for Monday night. 1. Justin Jefferson feasts vs. Bills' defense Accountability time: I was wildly off the mark with my prediction for Justin Jefferson's yardage total against the Lions last week . To be fair, even the most pessimistic of skeptics didn't expect the passing game to be that shaky. Luckily for Jefferson, Carson Wentz may be on his way to save him. Kyler Murray is battling through a hamstring injury and was officially ruled out for Week 9 on Thursday. Head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed that Wentz will start against the Bills on Monday, while Murray remains "week-to-week," according to ESPN 's Kevin Seifert. If there's one thing Wentz does well, it's getting Jefferson involved early and often. Jefferson averages 9.3 targets and 89.1 receiving yards per game with Wentz under center through seven games. Compare that to 7.6 targets and 52 yards per game in three full games with Murray. Wentz will need to feed his star wideout if the Vikings want to end the night with a statement win. 2. Vikings' defense holds the Bills to less than 300 total yards This one is a swing, but I'm betting on the Vikings defense to defend their home turf against one of the best offensive units in the NFL. Josh Allen and the Bills are averaging 393.1 total yards per game, trailing only the Lions. The Vikings defense, meanwhile, allows the second-fewest yards per game at only 271.6.Getting to Allen early while preventing him from taking off will be the key. This will be one of their hardest challenges of the year, but I'm certain defensive coordinator Brian Flores and his unit are preparing hard for this one. The Vikings need DC Brian Flores to give his best performance of the season so far when they face the Bills on Monday. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Minnesota's defense put up a strong effort in Detroit last week, but a total lack of help from the offense eventually opened the door for Jahmyr Gibbs to ice the game. A better offensive performance and home-field advantage should keep the unit energized. The Vikings will need it against a loaded offense led by Allen and James Cook. 3. Carson Wentz throws for Vikings' season-high in yardage The ingredients for a Wentz legacy performance are starting to add up. The Vikings' passing game needs a serious boost;o Jefferson and Jordan Addison need targets, and head coach Kevin O'Connell almost certainly wants to silence the doubts around his offensive scheme. Time to let it rip. The Bills' 254.7 passing yards allowed per game are the third-highest total in the NFL this season, an average higher than any passing performance we've seen this year from a Vikings passer. Murray's 247 yards against the Dolphins is currently the season high, but I think that changes Monday. Mark me down for Wentz over 250 through the air. away.headline: Bills' Joe Brady shares WR DJ Moore injury update
away.blurb: When asked what it meant to him to be back out there, he was quick to respond. "Everything!" "Meant everything. I got the jitters when I first stepped on the field and then I got the jitters out even more when I fumbled and I was like, 'All right, now it's time to really lock back in and get going,'" the WR1 shared . "So, I was nervous at first and then went out there and just was like, 'All right, this is the game that I love and was good.'" Head coach Joe Brady spoke to the impact that Moore's return had as well as his importance to the Buffalo offense. He limped off the field after that play, and went to the medical tent to get checked out, before returning. Though he again showed a limp leaving the field after the game, he says he is okay. "You play a lot of games in this league. You're nervous because of coming back from the injury or just cuz you haven't been out there," he added. "It's more because of the injury and not being out there. So, l'm like, 'Dang, am I in game shape?' And today I found out I was." away.headline: Ravens Get Disappointing Injury Update on Tyler Huntley After Loss to Bills: Report
away.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens had a rough afternoon, starting with the first offensive play of the game when quarterback Lamar Jackson hit Bills defender Greg Rousseau's arm, causing Jackson to suffer a thumb injury and not return. Jackson's backup, Tyler Huntley , also didn't last long. Huntley suffered a toe injury in the first half and didn't return. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Sunday that Huntley suffered a turf toe injury. Huntley and Jackson could both miss time, and Jackson is confirmed out for at least four weeks. Head coach Jesse Minter said postgame that Jackson will be placed on injured reserve and will undergo surgery on his right thumb. Ravens Offensive Weapon Set to Return Thursday Night vs Jags Ravens Get Disappointing Injury Update on Tyler Huntley After Loss to Bills: Report Unlock the latest Heavy on Ravens news — direct to your inbox. This was Jackson first game back after he suffered an ankle injury against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4 and missed the last three games. "Ravens QB Tyler "Snoop" Huntley suffered what is thought to be a turf toe injury today at Buffalo, per source," Schefter wrote on X. "He is expected to undergo an MRI tomorrow to determine how much time if any he could miss." Ravens Could Be Down Jackson and Huntley for a While The Ravens turned to quarterback Joe Fagnano after losing Huntley, and he had a tough afternoon, completing 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and one interception. Minter also said, "We'll see" on whether Jackson will miss the rest of the season. Huntley has started three games this season, and the Ravens are 1-2. The Ravens beat the Falcons in his first start of the season but lost the last two against the Browns and Bengals. Losing your starting quarterback and backup in the same game is never good. It's even worse when this happens during a short week. The Ravens will have a quick turnaround as they host the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night. The Jaguars are coming off a 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday to move to 5-2. Baltimore might not have a chance to play Huntley even if he can go, since it's hard to come back from an injury on a shorter week with less than four full days to recover. It will also be difficult for the Ravens to bring in a quarterback to play on Thursday, even if they lack confidence in Fagnano. The Ravens might have to get by with Fagnano starting on Thursday, then reevaluate options when they have about 10 days off between their games against the Jaguars and the Los Angeles Chargers on Nov. 16. home.headline: Vikings-Bills First Injury Report
home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray being out is the big news and he will not play on Monday night. Theo Jackson also did not practice on Thursday and seems more questionable whether he’ll play or not. Kevin O’Connell said they have other safeties like Jay Ward who could play in Jackson’s absence and a few others are possbilities to be active on Monday night if need be as well. The rest of the injuries appear to be more of the ‘playing through it’ variety and don’t seem like they’ll keep those players out on Monday night. For the Bills, a laundry list of players on the injury report including three offensive line starters. Starting left tackle Dion Dawkins did not practice Thursday with a rib injury, nor did starting guard Alec Andreesen, with an ankle injury. Right tackle Spencer Brown was limited with a back issue. We’ll see how it plays out with injury updates tomorrow and Saturday. Dawkins was a surprise addition to the injury report as he appeared to come out of Sunday's game intact. He sat out the last possession, missing four snaps, but so did Allen and starting center Connor McGovern. Veteran guard Austin Corbett, who subbed in for the Allen touchdown rush, would start on Monday if Anderson is unavailable. Coleman is limited by a shoulder, which explains the red non-contact jersey he dawned on Thursday. It's unknown at which point in the game the injury occurred.
